# lich

`lich` is an **ADE (agentic development environment) for AI coding agents**; the agents it runs, Claude Code,
Codex and the rest, are what this codebase calls harnesses. A pure-Go backend drives a native window, `native/`
(Gio, libghostty-vt), over a loopback contract (`docs/native-window.md`). It is built for
other developers to use, not only its author: docs, errors and defaults answer to a stranger. Linux first;
Windows and macOS are supported, with no hardware here for either.

**This file is instruction, not documentation.** Rules, gates and the workflow live here. What the project *is*
lives in the code, `docs/` and `CHANGELOG.md` — never restate any of it here.

## Where things are written down

- **Deliberate limits and the traps they set**: `docs/ceilings.md`. Read it before changing anything a session
  touches — spawn and naming, hooks, transcripts and cost, git and worktree flows, persistence, plugin install.
  A change that sets a new trap or closes an old one moves that file in the same PR.
- **Session hooks**: `docs/hooks/` is the canonical, contract-first spec. lich owns the server side; the scripts
  live in the companion repo `lichdotdev/lich-plugin`, so an endpoint or payload change breaks a repo this one
  cannot see — move the contract first, then both sides.
- **Every task**: `task --list`. `native/slice.sh` runs a window on its own backend, DB and port; it never
  touches an installed lich's workspace. That isolation is one `pkill` wide: a pattern like `lich` matches the
  running lich's own backend, and killing it ends every session under it. Kill a rig by the PID it was
  launched with.
- **Building, a rig window and the local gate from an agent session**: `.claude/skills/lich-build-dev/`, the
  procedure and the traps of running them inside the user's own lich.
- **Translations**: two independent languages, the interface and the prompt language (what lich and
  lich-plugin hand agents). `.claude/skills/lich-i18n/` maps where a string lands and every point a new
  language touches, and the rules for writing a message.
- **How the window looks**: `native/DESIGN.md`, the tokens, button sizes, spacing and screen layout. Read it
  before drawing or changing UI; a pattern corrected in review lands there in the same PR.
- **User-facing feature history**: `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Rules of the codebase

- Go 1.27, pure Go: `CGO_ENABLED=0` and a fully static binary are a constraint, not a default. The window,
  `native/`, is the one exception: its own Go module and binary, `lich-native`, built with cgo (Gio,
  libghostty-vt), talking to the backend only over RPC, `/events`, `/ws` and `/blob`, never importing
  `internal/` (`docs/native-window.md`).
- OS-specific code is selected by build tags behind small seams, never by runtime checks — the PTY is the model
  (`internal/terminal`).
- No literal user-visible or agent-facing text: a string a person reads on a lich screen, or that lich types
  into a session, goes through the catalogs and lands in **every** locale in the same PR (`lich-i18n` skill).
  English is the source; tests stay English. Error text, `CHANGELOG.md`, MCP tool descriptions and CLI help
  stay English by design; the What's new dialog reads a release's translations from `changelog/<locale>.md`.
- An RPC method is declared once in `api` and exposed with `rpc.Handle` in `internal/routes`: the backend,
  `lich` and `native/backend` compile against that one declaration, and `api/testdata/contract.golden` records
  its shape (`go test ./api -update` after a change meant to move it). Its options are one struct, never
  positional arguments. The service method it routes has the method's own shape,
  `func(context.Context, Options) (Result, error)`, and the route hands it over as `s.Method`, no closure; one
  that cannot fail keeps its body in an unexported method its own package calls. An `/events` event is declared there too, emitted with `events.Send` and read with
  `backend.Decode`. There is no codegen.
- A fact more than one place shows (git status, a pull request, plan quota, a session's profile or status) has
  one store per window, fed by one reader, and every screen reads that store. A change to the fact reaches the
  store as an event on `/events`, emitted by the backend once the change is true (after the respawn, not before),
  never as a call from the code that made the change into the screens that show it. Writer emits, store listens,
  screens read: a new screen subscribes and nothing upstream learns it exists.

## Local Gate (before every commit / PR)

- **Run from inside a lich session, the gate runs in a memory jail** (Linux, systemd): an unbounded
  `go test ./...`, the cross-compile loop and the native build starve the lich you are running in
  (`docs/ceilings.md` › the gate kills the window). Run each step sequentially through:
  `T=/var/tmp/lich-gate; mkdir -p $T; systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=2G --nice=10 env GOTMPDIR=$T TMPDIR=$T GOFLAGS=-p=2 <step>`.
  Never start two gate steps at once. The directory stays short: `go test` hands GOTMPDIR to the tests as
  their TMPDIR, and a deeper one pushes the sandbox suite's Unix sockets past the 108-byte path limit.
- `gofmt -l .` clean (fix with `gofmt -w .`) and `go vet ./...` clean.
- `go test ./...` green.
- From `native/`, `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` clean, with `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` pointing at a
  libghostty-vt built from the commit in `native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT` (`native/slice.sh` says how). Changed what it
  draws? Take a `-shot` and look at it; the maintainer's review in a real window is the one to trust.
- Shipped anything a user can see? Its `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` entry lands in the same PR — the release notes
  are read from there, so an entry written later is an entry that missed its release.
- Touched an OS seam or a `_test.go` build tag? Run the same cross-compile loop CI runs:
  `for os in linux darwin windows; do GOOS=$os go build ./... && GOOS=$os go vet ./...; done`
  Cross-compiling only proves it builds; the backend suite runs on real Windows and macOS runners on every PR,
  and that is the answer to trust.

## Hard Invariants

Non-negotiable rules. A violation means the work is not done.

1. **Test coverage ≥ 80%** on the backend. CI fails below the bar on its total
   (`.github/scripts/go-test-summary.sh`). An exclusion goes in that script, never into a skipped test.
   OS/framework boundaries (the PTY, the zenity subprocesses, WebSocket wiring, the `main` bootstrap) are the
   documented exception: cover the pure logic and leave the boundary itself alone.
2. **Tests answer to the contract, never the other way round.** Never weaken, skip, delete or rewrite a test to buy
   a green run or a coverage number. A test may change for exactly two reasons: the contract changed, or the test
   asserted something the contract never promised — name which one in the diff. When in doubt, change the product,
   not the test.
3. **A flake is a bug, and it has a root cause.** Never re-run CI until it goes green, never dismiss a failure as
   "unrelated" without proving it. Reproduce (`go test -count=200 -run TestX ./pkg/`), fix the cause, and measure
   the failure rate before and after.
4. **Clean code.** Small focused functions (< 50 lines); cohesive files (200–400 lines typical, 800 max); no
   nesting deeper than 4 levels; comments only for the *why*; errors handled explicitly, never swallowed; no magic
   values; no secrets in source.
5. **A session feature is traced across every provider.** `internal/providers.Registry` is the checklist —
   Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, opencode, oh-my-pi, Crush, Cursor CLI, Kiro CLI. Anything a session
   touches (spawn flags, hooks, resume, transcripts, plugin install, MCP) is designed against all eight, and
   `docs/adding-a-provider.md` is the map of every file one lands in. Equal behaviour is not always possible —
   but the gap must be deliberate and written down in the same PR, in both places: a `docs/ceilings.md` bullet
   naming which providers are out and why, and a row in the Provider support table of `README.md` and each
   `README.<lang>.md`, written in what the user sees. A feature that silently works on a single provider is not
   done, and neither is one whose gap only a contributor can find.

## Releases

The version comes from the git tag (`git describe` in the Taskfile, env `VERSION` overrides) and is injected into
`build/linux/nfpm/nfpm.yaml` — never hand-edit it there. Before tagging:

- [ ] Local gate green, backend with `-race`.
- [ ] Cut the `CHANGELOG.md` section the Keep a Changelog way: `[Unreleased]` stays at the top, emptied, and its
      entries move under a new `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading — bracketed, ISO date, no `v`: the release job
      greps `^## \[X.Y.Z\]` and ships empty notes if it misses. Keep the sections in their canonical order
      (Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security), and refresh the compare links, `[Unreleased]`
      included.
- [ ] Translate the cut section for the What's new dialog with the `lich-changelog-i18n` skill, alert blocks
      included, in the same commit: `TestTranslations` (`internal/patchnotes`) fails until every
      `changelog/<locale>.md` holds this release.
- [ ] Want the release to announce itself? Write GitHub alert blocks right under its heading, before the first
      `###`: `> [!IMPORTANT]` is the release's headline and opens the What's new dialog (one per release — a
      second one is demoted to a callout, which is the signal to fold it into the groups); `> [!WARNING]` is
      something the reader must do or avoid; `> [!NOTE]` is a detail worth a line. One or two sentences each,
      opening with a bold sentence that names its audience. The same blocks render as callouts on the release
      page. Most releases carry none.
- [ ] Push the `vX.Y.Z` tag — `.github/workflows/release.yml` does the rest, and reads the notes from that section.

# Claude Code

`claude` (`internal/providers.Registry`), the default provider and the companion plugin's home. Its config
directory is `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `~/.claude`, with the account in `~/.claude.json` beside it. A
conversation is one JSONL at `projects/<slug>/<id>.jsonl`, and a sub-agent's is a file of its own under
`projects/<slug>/<id>/subagents/`. The limits these sit under are in [`../ceilings.md`](../ceilings.md).

## Spawn

lich appends to the agent's system prompt (`internal/terminal/command.go`, `briefingFlags` →
`relay.SpawnBriefing`): a session is spawned with `--append-system-prompt` carrying lich's own briefing, so text
the user never wrote is in every session's prompt and in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`.

In a fresh worktree Claude Code asks whether the folder is trusted, and text typed into that question with an
Enter behind it exits the CLI (measured 2026-10-08), which is why the start gate waits for its session-start
report (`internal/terminal/startgate.go`).

Trust (`internal/claudeprofile/trust.go`): Personal needs nothing carried, since Claude Code finds the answer
for a worktree in its main checkout and for a folder in its parents (measured on 2.1.302). A confined session
skips the question with `CLAUDE_CODE_SANDBOXED=1`.

A misspelled effort level warns and runs at the default. On resume the model comes back from the conversation
(2.1.274) and the effort does not: it resumes on the saved default that Claude Code's own `/effort` writes
(`settings.json`), so a level changed inside the session survives while one lich set at birth falls back.

Ultracode (`ultracodeArgs`) is a Claude Code mode, standing multi-agent workflow orchestration, and no other
provider has one, so `lich open --ultracode` and `open_session`'s `ultracode` are refused for every other kind
and Settings offers the switch on Claude Code alone. lich passes it as `--settings '{"ultracode":true}'` rather
than `--effort ultracode`, which pins the effort to xhigh. Claude Code drops it on `--resume` (measured on
2.1.288), so unlike the model and effort it is passed on every spawn, and a fork inherits it from the session
whose conversation it branches.

## Hooks

Claude Code is the only provider that says what a session is waiting for
(`statusRung` in `native/cmd/lich-native/statusrung.go`; the mapping table is in
[`../hooks/session-state.md`](../hooks/session-state.md)). Its `Notification` carries a `message` written for a
human, so the card reads "Claude needs your permission to use Bash".

A `/resume` typed inside Claude Code reports the new conversation at the switch (measured 2026-10-17), so the
two-cards-one-conversation warning arrives at once.

## Transcript & cost

The full readout: per-turn token counts, and the window its mod reports, else one named from the model
(`windowForModel`). The running model the card's tooltip names is the assistant's `message.model`. The cache line
under the window splits the same line's input into `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens` and
`input_tokens`, and goes away after a compaction until the next assistant line.

A conversation lich spawned is told from a plain `claude` run by the name lich spawns it under
(`relay.IsRosterName` on the first `custom-title`), which covers the conversations whose rows were deleted before
the tombstones of schema version 8: measured on a real workspace, it marked 490 of the 539 Claude conversations
lich held no row for, and the 49 left had no title at all, which is a plain `claude` run. A new session is no
longer spawned under a name (`nameArgs`), so the name only tells apart the conversations born before that; the
tombstones cover every row deleted since.

## Plugin install

Driven through Claude Code's own plugin CLI (`internal/agentplugin`), so lich writes none of the files itself
and does not track the installed version in a marker line of its own.

## MCP

The session is handed lich's own MCP server on its command line (`--mcp-config`,
`providers.AcceptsMCPServer`), so a tool added here is in that session's list on the next spawn.

## Account

The plan gauge names the account a session spends (`internal/quota`, `Plan.Account`): lich answers Claude
Code's profile route with the credentials token. The usage route is the one Claude Code's own CLI polls.

A long-lived OAuth token (`claude setup-token`) carries `user:inference` alone, so the usage route answers it 403
and the gauge sends one `max_tokens: 1` message for the rate-limit headers on the response
(`internal/quota/claude.go`). That request carries Claude Code's system prompt verbatim because the API rejects an
OAuth token without it — the same coupling as the user agent, and it fails closed, as a failed reading. Headers
carry the two account-wide windows and no plan name, so such a session shows no model-scoped weekly cap and no
"Max 5x" badge.

## Profiles

A profile is a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` of its own with a real `claude auth login` (`internal/claudeprofile`). The
login the dialog starts is `claude auth login --claudeai`, which opens the browser itself and takes the callback
on a localhost port of its own (measured on 2.1.296); the address it prints, which redirects to a page that shows
a code, and the field that takes the code are for a browser that cannot reach this machine.

Shared through links (`internal/claudeprofile/profile.go`, `internal/profilestore/layout.go`): `settings.json`,
`CLAUDE.md`, `agents/`, `commands/`, `skills/`, `hooks/` and the marketplace clones (`plugins/marketplaces`) point
at Personal's, and Claude Code writes through a link to its target (measured on 2.1.296). The plugin set itself
(`installed_plugins.json`, `known_marketplaces.json`) is per profile, because an organization account may forbid
plugins Personal runs. An entry Personal gains after a profile was made is linked at that profile's next spawn. On
Windows the directories are junctions, but a file link needs Developer Mode: without it `settings.json` and
`CLAUDE.md` are copies, named on the profile (`copied`), and they drift from Personal's on the first edit to
either. A hard link was measured and drifts just the same, Claude Code replacing the file on write. The global
`.claude.json` is a copy everywhere, minus the account and its caches, since Claude Code replaces it through a
rename that would turn a link into a file anyway.

Trust in a profile: the copied `.claude.json` freezes the trust answers at its birth, so before each spawn into a
profile lich writes `hasTrustDialogAccepted` for the checkout's top when Personal trusts it or the main checkout
of the worktree it is. A folder outside any git checkout is not carried into a profile: lich asks git, not the
parents. The write is a read, an edit and a rename beside sessions that rewrite the same file; Claude Code
re-reads it before each write of its own (a key written mid-session survived its later writes), so the window
left is what either side writes between the other's read and rename.

The plugin cache (`internal/claudeprofile/plugincache.go`): before every spawn, and in the startup pass of the
lich plugin, each version a profile's `installed_plugins.json` names under its `plugins/cache` is moved into
`plugin_cache/` beside the profiles (or gives way to the copy already there) and replaced by a link to it. Claude
Code's orphan sweep, run at every session start, marks each cached version its own record does not name
(`.orphaned_at`) and deletes it once the mark is 14 days old, but it passes over a version that is a link, marking
and deleting nothing through it, and `plugin update`, `uninstall` and a reinstall over a link leave the store's
copy alone (all measured on 2.1.299, a plugin running from a linked version included). A version Claude Code
downloads stays a plain directory of the profile, which its own record protects, until the next spawn links it.
Personal's cache is Personal's alone and is left as it is, so a version both use is on disk twice. A profile made
when the whole cache was a link to Personal's is moved at its next spawn or lich start: each version it names is
copied from Personal's into the store, and one Personal's sweep already deleted stays missing. `.in_use` markers
of every profile running a version land in the store's copy, which a confined session reaches because the store
is bound read-write beside the profile (`internal/terminal/sandbox.go`). On Windows each version is a junction,
which Claude Code's sweep reads as a link too (read in the source, not run on Windows), and a version Windows will
not move while a file in it is open stays the profile's own until a later spawn. `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR`
moves Claude Code's whole `plugins/` directory, installed set, marketplaces and cache, not only the cache
(measured on 2.1.300), so a profile's spawn, login and plugin install drop it and a profile's plugins stay inside
its own directory; Personal keeps it, and lich reads Personal's installed set where it points
(`claudeprofile.PluginsDir`). A new profile seeds its marketplaces from, and links its clones to, Personal's
plugins directory where the variable points. A profile made before the variable was set keeps the
`plugins/marketplaces` link it was made with, and clones each marketplace again into a directory Personal no
longer reads; removing that link has the next spawn link it where the variable points.

The lich plugin follows Personal's (`internal/agentplugin/profiles.go`): `claude plugin install` installs into a
logged-out home (measured on 2.1.296), so every profile gets it, logged in or not. The pass lays each profile out
as a spawn would before asking its version (`EnsureShared`), which also moves a profile's plugin cache off
Personal's at a start. A profile's `plugin marketplace remove` deletes the marketplace clone it links to
Personal's (the plugin cache stays, measured on 2.1.296).

Continue in (`claudeprofile.MoveConversation`, `terminal.ContinueIn`) moves what Claude Code keys by the
conversation id: the transcript, its subagent directory, any file a hook filed beside it under the same name,
and `file-history/`, `session-env/` and `tasks/` under that id, the set a throwaway conversation left on 2.1.296,
which resumed with its history and checkpoints both ways. The prompt history (`history.jsonl`) and the project's
`lastSessionId` stay in the profile it left, so the arrow-up history does not follow. An async hook outlives the
Claude Code it ran for (its SessionEnd hook runs in a session of its own, measured on 2.1.304), so lich cannot
wait for it: a hook can file its entry again in the profile the conversation just left, and moving back replaces
that leftover instead of refusing. A move across filesystems copies, Windows volumes included. A card that has not
had its first prompt has no transcript yet, so it is not moved but started afresh in the target profile.

## Sandbox

Nothing provider-specific.

## Known limits

Unfold long pastes pastes twice wherever lich predicts the fold, because a repeat of the same text unfolds the
`[Pasted text #N +M lines]` chip. The prediction is Claude Code's rule copied from its 2.1.296 bundle (more than
800 characters, or more than `min(rows - 10, 2)` newlines, up to 100 000), and it assumes the paste goes to the
prompt.

A theme switch reaches it: Claude Code turns on mode 2031 (driven in a PTY).

name: lich-build-dev
description: Build, run and verify lich from an agent session without taking down the user's own lich window. Use before building anything (the Go binary, the native window in `native/`), before running a window on its own backend (`native/slice.sh`, `lich native`, `lich gallery`), before running tests or the local gate, and before verifying a UI change in a running lich.
---

# lich build, rig and local gate

What the gate *is* lives in the root `CLAUDE.md` › Local Gate; every task in `task --list`; the window in
`docs/native-window.md`; first-build prerequisites in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. This skill is the procedure for running
them from inside a lich session, and the traps that procedure avoids.

**You are running inside the user's live lich.** Every session on their screen, this one included, is a child of
its backend. Never `pkill`/`killall`/`kill` by pattern (`lich`, `lich-native`, `slice.sh`): the pattern matches
the user's own lich, and the backend's death takes every session down. Kill only a PID or process group you
started and wrote down.

## 1. First steps in a fresh worktree

```bash
W=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)       # use absolute paths from here on
which -a go                              # only mise paths (~/.local/share/mise/...)
# libghostty-vt: built once per machine at native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT; native/slice.sh's header says how
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$(dirname "$(find ~/.cache/lich-native-slice/libghostty-vt -name '*.pc' | head -1)")
```

## 2. The local gate, in order

One step at a time, each inside the memory jail from `CLAUDE.md` › Local Gate (`cap` below is that command):
gate steps run in parallel have killed the user's window. Never start two of these at once. Keep `$T`
short: `go test` hands it to the tests as their TMPDIR, and the sandbox suite's Unix sockets break past the
108-byte path limit.

```bash
W=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); T=/var/tmp/lich-gate; mkdir -p "$T"
cap() { systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=2G --nice=10 \
  env GOTMPDIR="$T" TMPDIR="$T" GOFLAGS=-p=2 "$@"; }
cd "$W" && pwd &&
  test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" &&
  cap go vet ./... &&
  cap go test ./... &&
cd "$W/native" && pwd &&
  test -z "$(gofmt -l .)" &&
  cap go vet ./... &&
  cap go test ./... &&
  echo GATE GREEN
```

- `native/` needs `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` from section 1; without it the cgo steps fail on a missing `libghostty-vt`.
- Touched an OS seam or a `_test.go` build tag: the cross-compile loop in `CLAUDE.md`, under `cap`.

## 3. A window on its own backend

`native/` is a separate Go module and binary (`docs/native-window.md`). Never point it at the user's lich: the
backend's `/events` and `/ws` serve one client each, so a native window on the user's backend takes the sockets
from their real window. `native/slice.sh` runs an isolated backend instead: its own config dir and DB
(`~/.cache/lich-native-slice/config`), port 47901, separate from the user's lich. The backend outlives the window, so its sessions survive between runs.

```bash
W=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); T=/var/tmp/lich-gate; mkdir -p "$T"
cap() { systemd-run --user --scope --quiet -p MemoryMax=6G -p MemorySwapMax=2G --nice=10 \
  env GOTMPDIR="$T" TMPDIR="$T" GOFLAGS=-p=2 "$@"; }
ss -ltnp 'sport = :47901'                       # empty, or a slice backend is already up (see below)
# PKG_CONFIG_PATH from section 1; this checkout's backend and window, built in the jail
cd "$W" && cap go build -o "$T/lich" . &&
cd "$W/native" && cap go build -o cmd/lich-native/lich-native ./cmd/lich-native &&
LICH_BIN="$T/lich" setsid "$W/native/slice.sh" "$W" > "$T/native.log" 2>&1 < /dev/null & echo $! > "$T/native.pid"
kill "$(cat "$T/native.pid")"                   # close the window: your PID only
"$W/native/slice.sh" stop                       # stop the slice backend and its sessions
```

- The argument opens that checkout as the project on the backend's first run; later runs reuse its projects.
- A slice backend already on 47901 is reused as is, whatever binary it runs. Backend code changed, or it is not
  yours? Ask before `slice.sh stop`: it may hold the user's review window and sessions.
- Without `LICH_BIN` the backend is the installed `lich` on PATH, enough when only `native/` changed.
- Drawing changed: `timeout 15 cmd/lich-native/lich-native -runtime
  ~/.cache/lich-native-slice/config/lich/runtime-dev.json -shot out.png -shot-after 4s` writes a frame; the
  window stays open after it, hence the `timeout`. It takes the backend's sockets for those seconds, so not
  while the user has a native window on the same backend. Look at the PNG; the user's review in a real window
  is the one to trust.
- The UI kit gallery (`native/cmd/ui-gallery`, every `native/ui` primitive, no backend and no libghostty-vt)
  is the place to review a primitive. Build it in the jail, `cap go build -o "$T/lich-gallery" ./cmd/ui-gallery`
  from `native/`, then open it with `LICH_GALLERY="$T/lich-gallery" "$T/lich" gallery` (a lich built from this
  checkout; the installed one may predate the command) or run it directly under `setsid`, writing its PID down.
  `-shot out.png` (with `-shot-after`, `-shot-height` for the whole scrolled page) writes a frame and exits.

## 4. Traps

- **rtk rewrites commands and fakes exit codes.** A rewritten command can print a clean summary and still exit
  non-zero, or the other way round. Prefix `rtk proxy` when the exit code or the full output matters. Output
  that looks cut is the same hook: `rtk proxy <cmd>`.
- **Read exit codes, not tails.** `| tail` hides the exit status; redirect to a log under `$T` and echo `$?`.
- **cwd drifts.** A failed `cd native && ...` leaves the shell in another directory, sometimes another
  checkout. Use `$W` and start a step with `pwd &&` when it matters.
- **Two Go toolchains.** mise exports `GOROOT`; a stray `/usr/bin/go` obeys it and fails intermittently with
  stdlib mismatches. `which -a go` must list only mise paths.
- **A rig needs its own HOME, not just its own config dir** (`internal/agentplugin.RepairRegistrations`). Every
  launch that is not `task dev` (`LICH_DEV`) or a `go run` binary repoints the provider MCP registrations it
  finds to its own executable, and those live under HOME, not under the config dir: `~/.cursor/mcp.json`,
  `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`, `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` and Kiro's agent. A built binary launched with
  only `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (or `APPDATA`) moved rewrites the user's real agents to point at a scratch binary that
  is deleted later. Give a rig its own `HOME` and `XDG_*` both, and check those files afterwards. Two side
  effects of that HOME: a `node` reached through a mise shim stops trusting the user's mise config and exits,
  so call the real binary (`mise which node`); and a rig given its own D-Bus (`dbus-run-session`, so its tray
  stays off the user's bar) activates portals and a notification daemon that outlive it, found by their
  `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and stopped by PID.
- **A plugin install from `task dev` registers the `lich` on PATH, not itself** (`internal/agentplugin/crush.go`,
  `resolveLichBinary`). Crush's, oh-my-pi's, Cursor's, Antigravity's and Kiro's registrations name the absolute
  path of the lich that wrote them, and under `go run` that path is the toolchain's cache binary, deleted when the
  run ends, so lich writes `lich` from PATH instead, recognising the cache by shape (`go-build*/b*/exe/*`) since
  the toolchain exports no marker. A dev install therefore points at whatever version is installed on the
  machine: harmless, because the registration is only the transport and a session reaches the lich its PTY's
  coordinates name, but not what the file appears to say. With no lich on PATH a dev install registers nothing:
  Crush, oh-my-pi, Antigravity and Kiro still get their hooks, and Cursor's install refuses outright.

description: Translate the latest release's CHANGELOG.md section into every interface language lich ships, adding it to changelog/<locale>.md, the files the What's new popup and the site's changelog pages read. # lich changelog translations

The What's new popup shows the running build's `CHANGELOG.md` section (`internal/patchnotes`). A user whose
interface language is not English reads it from `changelog/<locale>.md` instead, embedded in the binary
next to `CHANGELOG.md`. Each file holds **every translated release, newest first**: a build only reads its own
version, but the site's changelog page in that language lists them all and sends the reader to the English page
where they stop. `CHANGELOG.md` stays English and canonical; the release page reads it.

## When

Cutting a release (`CLAUDE.md` › Releases): once the section is under its `## [X.Y.Z] - YYYY-MM-DD` heading and
its text is final, run this before tagging, in the same commit. A fix to the released English text afterwards
means running it again.

## Steps

1. **Slice the source.** The release is the first `## [` heading in `CHANGELOG.md` below `## [Unreleased]`.
   Its section runs from that heading to the next `## ` heading.
2. **One file per locale, except English.** The locales are `prompt.Langs` (`internal/prompt/prompt.go`),
   file names are their tags as written there: `pt-BR.md`, `es.md`, `zh-CN.md`, `ja.md`, `ko.md`, `ru.md`.
   A language added to lich gets its file in the same PR.
3. **Add the translated section at the top of each file**, above the previous release, with a blank line
   between them, and nothing else: no `# Changelog` title, no `[Unreleased]`, no compare links. Running it again
   for the same release replaces that release's section, never adds a second one.
4. **Translate from the English**, never from another translation. The locales are independent, so each
   one can go to its own subagent in parallel, on a cheap model (Sonnet); hand each the English section and
   the rules below.
5. **Run the check** and finish only when it is green (needs nothing built):
   `go test -run TestTranslations ./internal/patchnotes`

## What stays in English, byte for byte

The parser and both windows read these, so `TestTranslations` fails when one is touched:

- The version heading, date included: `## [0.69.0] - 2026-10-16`.
- The group headings: `### Added`, `### Changed`, `### Deprecated`, `### Removed`, `### Fixed`,
  `### Security`. The windows translate the label on screen and color it by the English word.
- The alert openers: `> [!IMPORTANT]`, `> [!WARNING]`, `> [!NOTE]`. The text under them is translated, each
  line still starting with `> `.
- Every `code` span, exactly as written. Their order inside an item may follow the language's grammar.

## How to translate

- **Same structure.** Same groups in the same order, same number of `- ` items in each, same alert blocks.
  An item may wrap over as many lines as it needs; a blank line between items is fine; a blank line inside
  an item ends it.
- **The bold lead-in stays bold.** `**The native window opens on Windows.**` becomes one `**…**` in the
  translation, and the rest of the item follows it as plain text. No bold, italics or links the English
  does not have.
- **Names stay names:** lich, the providers (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, opencode, oh-my-pi, Crush,
  Cursor CLI, Kiro CLI), OS and app names (Linux, Windows, macOS, Wayland, Terminal.app), commands and key
  names, plus the rest of `lich-i18n`'s literal list.
- **Interface words match the interface.** A setting, menu or button named in the English (Settings ›
  Notifications, Remove worktree, Undo) is written the way that language's catalog shows it on
  screen: look it up in `native/i18n/locales/<lang>/` instead of translating it afresh. `›` stays as the path separator.
- **Plain release-note register** for that language, written for a developer: what changed for them, in
  the same tone and length as the English. Do not add, drop or explain.

## If the check fails

- `version headings = …`: the file does not open with the latest release, skips one, or holds one twice.
  Put the latest release's section at the top, once, from step 1.
- `N groups` / `N items`: an item was merged, split or lost, often a blank line inside an item.
- `group N is "…"`: a `### ` heading was translated.
- `code spans …` or `bold markers …`: a code span was changed or a `**` was lost; the message prints the
  item.

The check is the contract. Fix the translation, never the test.

# lich i18n

lich has two languages that never derive from each other:

- **Interface language**: lich's own screens. The catalogs are in `native/i18n/locales/`, chosen in
  Settings › General and stored in the global setting `lich.appearance.language`; the window follows the
  system's language until one is picked.
- **Prompt language**: every word lich hands an agent (spawn briefing, `[lich]` relay notes, nudges,
  merge notices, MCP and CLI results, prompts the window types into a PTY, lich-plugin's mod text).
  Stored as the global `prompt.language` setting, exported to every session as `LICH_PROMPT_LANG`.

This skill is the map of *where* a change lands, and the rules for writing a message. Start by deciding
which job this is.

## Writing a message

- **Keys** are `<namespace>.<component>.<what>`, camelCase (`sidebar.newFolderDialog.title`). A key names
  the meaning, never the English words. A message goes to `common` only once a second namespace needs it.
- **One sentence, one key.** Never build a sentence from fragments or concatenation: word order differs
  between languages. Values go in through named placeholders, `"Close {name}"` with
  `i18n.T("...", i18n.Args{"name": name})`. `{` in a message is always a placeholder.
- **Plurals** are an object of CLDR forms, `{ "one": "{count} file", "other": "{count} files" }`, picked
  from the int `count` (`plural.go`). Never branch on `n == 1` at the call. Portuguese counts 0 as `one`.
- **Not translated:** backend error text (only the sentence around it is), `CHANGELOG.md` (the What's new
  dialog reads its translations from `changelog/<locale>.md`, written by the `lich-changelog-i18n` skill at
  release time), identifiers and names (providers, branches, commands, file paths, `lich`, `Claude Code`),
  keyboard shortcuts, and a test's fixture data.

## Job 1: a feature adds or changes text

Classify every string first. Who reads it?

| Reader | Where it goes | Language |
|---|---|---|
| The user, on a lich screen | `native/i18n/locales/<lang>/<namespace>.json`, read with `i18n.T()` | interface |
| An agent, composed in Go (relay, briefing, notices, MCP/CLI output) | a field of `prompt.Catalog` (`internal/prompt/catalog.go`) | prompt |
| An agent, typed by the window into a PTY | `native/i18n/locales/<lang>/prompts.json`, read with `i18n.Prompt()` | prompt |
| An agent, added by a lich-plugin mod | `hooks/prompt-text.js` in `lichdotdev/lich-plugin` | prompt |
| The user, in the What's new dialog | `changelog/<locale>.md`, one release, written by the `lich-changelog-i18n` skill when a release is cut | interface |
| Nobody localizes it | backend error text, `CHANGELOG.md`, MCP tool descriptions, CLI `--help`, identifiers | none |

Then, in the same PR:

1. **English is the source.** Add the key to `native/i18n/locales/en/*` (or the `en.go` field) with the
   exact text.
2. **Every locale gets it.** One entry per file in `native/i18n/locales/*/` and per
   `internal/prompt/<lang>.go`. `TestEveryLocaleMatchesEnglish` fails on a missing key or placeholder;
   `TestCatalogParity` fails on an empty Go field or mismatched verbs.
   Translate from English, never from another translation.
3. **Literal in every locale:** `[lich]`, tool and CLI names (`send_to_session`, `wait_for_answer`,
   `reply_to_session`, `open_session`, `close_session`, `list_worktrees`, `"$LICH_BIN" reply|wait`,
   `lich send`, `gh pr create`), ticket ids, status enums (`pending`, `answered`, `unread`, ...),
   parameter names, product names, key names, `{placeholders}` and Go format verbs.
4. **Text lich matches by equality** (`resumePrompt` is the precedent: persisted, then compared) must
   match the text of *any* locale: `slices.ContainsFunc(prompt.Langs, ...)`. A row written under one
   language is read back under another.
5. **Out-of-process text** (`internal/cli`, plugin hooks) reads `LICH_PROMPT_LANG`, fixed at spawn. If
   the new text only reaches sessions born after a change, that is the existing ceiling; don't add a
   second mechanism.
6. **Tests stay in English.** Assert another locale with `i18n.SetCurrent` / `i18n.In` / a `prompt.Langs`
   loop, never by editing an English assertion.
7. **Provider symmetry.** Prompt text reaches all eight providers through the relay. The spawn briefing
   only exists where `docs/ceilings.md` says it does; a gap that grows goes there and in every README
   provider table.

### In the window's code

- Read a key at layout, never into a package-level `const` or `var`: Gio draws every frame, so a label
  that reads `i18n.T` while it lays out changes language on the next one. A table built at init (the
  settings index, the hotkeys) holds keys and resolves them when drawn; a settings row names
  `titleKey`/`alsoKey`/`groupKey` and is read through `titleText`/`alsoText`/`groupText`.
- `go:embed` cannot leave the `native/` module: the catalogs live under it.
- `TestEveryLocaleMatchesEnglish` (`native/i18n`) is the parity check, keys and placeholders;
  `TestEveryKeyTheSourceNamesIsInTheCatalog` (`native/cmd/lich-native`) fails on a literal key no catalog
  has. Write the key literally at the call so that test sees it.
- Tests stay English: nothing sets the interface language under `go test`. Assert another locale with
  `i18n.SetCurrent` / `i18n.In`, and set it back.

## Job 2: add a language

Pick the BCP 47 tag first (`es`, `zh-CN`, `pt-BR`); the same string is the window's `Locale`, the Go `Lang`, the
setting value, `LICH_PROMPT_LANG` and the plugin catalog key. Then touch every point below. Append the new
language at the **end** of every list so parallel additions merge as a union.

**Window** (`native/i18n/`)
- `i18n.go`: a `Locale` const, `Locales` (append), its name in itself in `Name` (`Español`, `简体中文`).
  `Match` needs no change unless the language's script or region rules differ from "exact tag, then
  language prefix".
- `locales/<tag-lowercase>/`: one JSON file per namespace in `locales/en/` (list it, don't remember it),
  every key English has.
- Plurals: write the CLDR forms the language uses; a language with forms other than one/other extends
  `pluralForm` (`plural.go`), as Russian does.

**Backend** (`internal/prompt/`)
- `prompt.go`: a `Lang` const, `Langs` (append), the `catalogs` map.
- `<tag>.go`: a full `Catalog`, including its `isOne` rule. `Plural` has only `One`/`Other`: a language
  with more CLDR forms (Russian, Arabic, Polish) extends `Plural` and `Pick` in the same PR.
- The spawn briefing must stay cmd.exe-safe (no `"` or `<>`); `compose_lang_test.go` checks every
  `Langs` entry, so a new language is covered once it is in `Langs`.
- Tests that loop `prompt.Langs` cover it automatically; add a language-specific case where the pt-BR
  or es one exists (`prompt_test.go`, `internal/cli/text_lang_test.go`, `internal/drop/notice_lang_test.go`,
  `internal/store/prompt_language_test.go`, `internal/terminal/prompt_language*_test.go`).

**Docs**
- `docs/hooks/README.md`: the accepted `LICH_PROMPT_LANG` values.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` › Added.
- `changelog/<locale>.md`: the latest release translated with the `lich-changelog-i18n` skill;
  `TestTranslations` (`internal/patchnotes`) fails until it exists.
- README.md and each README.<lang>.md only if they enumerate languages.

**Companion repo** `lichdotdev/lich-plugin` (separate PR, after lich's)
- `hooks/prompt-text.js`: a catalog object registered under the exact tag.
- `tests/prompt-text.test.mjs`: parity, literals, one render per hook for the new tag.
- The mod engine never follows `$` across an import: hooks read `$.env.get("LICH_PROMPT_LANG")` at the
  call site and pass the string to `promptLang(tag)`. Run **both** `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` and
  `claude plugin test .`; only the second loads the mods the way Claude Code does.
- The plugin text reaches users only after a plugin release.

## Splitting the work across agents

A new language is one agent per repo side, not one per namespace: the catalogs are read best as a whole,
and the registration points are few. Converting untranslated code is the opposite: one agent per folder,
since folders don't overlap. Agents working in parallel conflict only on the registration lists
(`Locales`, `Langs`), and those resolve as a union.

## Done means

- The Local Gate in the root `CLAUDE.md` is green.
- No existing test assertion changed.
- `go test ./internal/prompt/` and, from `native/`, `go test ./i18n/ ./cmd/lich-native/` pass.
- The new language was looked at in a running window (`lich-build-dev` skill): both selects, a session
  spawned after the switch, and one relay note.

Claude Code, Codex, opencode o el agente que ya usas, cada uno en su propio worktree, todos en una sola ventana.

## Funciones
### Agentes lado a lado Pon las sesiones en un grupo y lich acomoda los paneles por ti. Mira de un vistazo cuál está ocupada, cuál te está esperando y cuánto contexto le queda.
### Un worktree por tarea, sin preparar nada Crea una sesión a partir de cualquier rama base y lich le copia tus archivos `.env` y le asigna un puerto libre para el servidor de desarrollo. Tus cambios sin commitear pueden venir con ella.
### Revisa el diff, comenta las líneas Lee lo que cambió el agente junto a su sesión, comenta las líneas que necesitan retoque y devuelve todas las notas como un solo prompt.
### Señala la página, díselo al agente El agente maneja un navegador en una pestaña junto a su sesión, y tú usas la misma página. Señala lo que está mal, deja una nota encima y envía todas las notas de vuelta en un solo prompt.
### Pull requests sin el navegador Abre un pull request, pídele al agente de la rama que lo escriba, revísalo inline y fusiónalo, todo desde la misma ventana.
### Hazlo tuyo Importa un tema como JSON o instala uno desde un repositorio git. [Docs →](docs/themes.md)

Ninguna de estas diferencias es un descuido, y [`docs/ceilings.md`](docs/ceilings.md) cuenta qué se midió detrás de cada una. ## Configuración - **Proveedores.** En Ajustes › Proveedores defines la ruta del binario de cada agente y el predeterminado para todos los proyectos; un proyecto puede elegir el suyo. Si no defines ninguna ruta, lich ejecuta el primer binario que encuentre en el `PATH` de tu login shell, y `lich doctor` avisa cuando hay más de una versión. - **Pie de ventana.** En Ajustes › Apariencia, arrastra sus elementos para elegir qué muestra. El costo arranca oculto, porque esa cifra solo tiene sentido si pagas por token. - **Worktrees.** Con un archivo `.worktreeinclude` en el proyecto eliges qué archivos ignorados por git se copian a cada worktree nuevo. - **Hooks de sesión.** Instala el [plugin de lich](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich-plugin) desde Ajustes y cada sesión le pone título a su propia tarjeta y refresca el estado de git en cuanto escribe un archivo. - **Scripts.** En [docs/stability.md](docs/stability.md) está escrito en qué partes de lich puedes apoyarte desde un script. ## Privacidad y actualizaciones Todo corre en tu máquina: sin cuenta, sin login, sin telemetría. lich solo se conecta a la red para esto: - **Actualizaciones**: consulta la última versión en GitHub Releases al arrancar y cada hora, y la lista de versiones del plugin de lich al arrancar. - **Uso del plan**: el endpoint de uso de cada proveedor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, OpenCode Go), con el mismo login que ya usa el agente, como mucho cada cinco minutos. El plan de Antigravity se lee del propio `agy`. - **Precios**: la tabla pública de precios de LiteLLM en GitHub, una sola vez por cada modelo que no esté en la tabla que trae lich. El instalador de Windows se actualiza en el lugar; Homebrew, Scoop, AUR y los paquetes de Linux se actualizan con su gestor de paquetes, y lich te da el comando. ¿Algo no funciona? `lich doctor` revisa tu instalación y `lich rage` junta un reporte de bug en un solo archivo sin subir nada. Antes de que adjuntes el archivo de log, Ajustes › Ayuda te dice qué contiene (rutas, nombres de proyectos y de ramas, tu login de gh, nunca un token de sesión). Los bugs y los pedidos de funciones van a [Issues](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/issues); lo que cambió en cada versión está en [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Compilar desde el código fuente lich son dos binarios: `lich`, un backend estático en Go puro, y `lich-native`, la ventana, compilada con cgo desde `native/`. Necesitas **Go 1.27.0+** y **[Task](https://taskfile.dev)**; la ventana suma un toolchain de C, los paquetes de sistema de Gio y una `libghostty-vt` compilada desde el commit en `native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT`. [`native/slice.sh`](native/slice.sh) explica cómo, y [`docs/native-window.md`](docs/native-window.md) describe la ventana. ```bash task build # binario del backend -> bin/lich task build:native # ventana -> bin/lich-native task run # compila + ejecuta task test # suites de Go task package # .deb + .rpm + Arch .pkg.tar.zst en bin/ (requiere nfpm) ``` Sumar otro agente toca una docena de archivos repartidos en dos repositorios: [`docs/adding-a-provider.md`](docs/adding-a-provider.md) es el mapa. ## Patrocinadores lich lo escribe y lo mantiene una sola persona. El patrocinio paga el tiempo que se le dedica y mantiene el proyecto independiente: la app no tiene una versión de pago y no la va a tener. ## 機能
### エージェントを並べて動かす セッションを分割画面に置けば、ペインの配置は lich が決めます。どのセッションが作業中で、どれがあなたの返事を待っていて、コンテキストがどれだけ残っているかが、ひと目でわかります。
### タスクごとのワークツリー、準備はいりません 好きなベースブランチからセッションを分岐すると、lich が `.env` ファイルをコピーし、空いている開発サーバー用のポートを割り当てます。コミット前の作業も持ち込めます。
### 差分を読んで、行にコメントする エージェントが変更した内容をセッションの隣で読み、直したい行にコメントして、すべてのメモを1つのプロンプトとして送り返せます。
### ページを指して、エージェントに伝える エージェントはセッションの隣のタブでブラウザを操作し、あなたも同じページを使えます。おかしい箇所を指してメモを残し、すべてのメモを 1 つのプロンプトとして送り返します。
### ブラウザなしでプルリクエスト プルリクエストを開き、そのブランチのエージェントに書いてもらい、インラインでレビューして、マージするまで、同じウィンドウで完結します。
### 自分好みに テーマを JSON でインポートするか、git リポジトリからインストールできます。 [ドキュメント →](docs/themes.md)
ほかにも、こんなことができます。 - **仕事を任せ合うセッション。** あるエージェントが別のセッションにタスクを渡し、答えを受け取れます。シェルからも `lich` コマンドで同じことができます（[ドキュメント](docs/cli.md)）。 - **サンドボックス内のエージェント。** ssh キーも認証情報もほかのリポジトリも見えないサンドボックスの中なら、エージェントに権限確認をスキップさせても安心です（[限界](docs/ceilings.md)）。 - **開発サーバーをサイドバーに。** プロジェクトで動かし続けるものを保存しておけば、ワンクリックで起動・停止できます。 - **なんでも見つかる。** `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K` で、名前やセッション内で話した内容からセッションにジャンプできます。 - **出番がわかる。** セッションがあなたの入力を待っているときは、デスクトップ通知が届きます。 ## インストール ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lichdotdev/lich/main/install.sh | sh ``` 1行で、ディストリビューションを判別し、ダウンロードを検証して、パッケージマネージャーで lich をインストールします。 | プラットフォーム | 入手方法 | | --- | --- | | **Linux** | 上記の `install.sh`、または AUR の [`lich-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/lich-bin) (`yay -S lich-bin`)。`zenity` と glibc 2.34 以上が必要です（Debian 12、Ubuntu 22.04、RHEL 9 以降）。 | | **macOS** | `brew install --cask lichdotdev/tap/lich` | | **Windows** | [Releases](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases) のインストーラーまたはポータブル zip、または `scoop install https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases/latest/download/lich.json` | macOS と Windows のビルドはまだ署名されていないため、Releases からダウンロードすると Gatekeeper や SmartScreen の警告が出ます。Homebrew でインストールすれば Gatekeeper の確認は出ません。 ディストリビューション別のパッケージ、Linux の tarball、quarantine 属性の外し方、 古い Homebrew formula からのアップグレードは [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) にあります。 ## はじめに 1. **プロジェクトを開きます。** タブバーの `+` を押すと、最近閉じたプロジェクトの一覧と フォルダー選択ダイアログが出ます。git リポジトリを選んでください。 2. **使うエージェントを選びます。** 初回起動時に、マシン上で見つかったエージェントが一覧されます。 設定 › プロバイダーで、既定のエージェントと各バイナリのパスを設定できます。 3. **セッションを開始します。** *新規セッション* で、プロジェクト内でエージェントが開きます。 各チェックアウトのヘッダーにある `+` からは、好きなエージェントや通常のターミナルを、そのチェックアウトで開けます。 4. **ワークツリーを作ります** *(任意)*。どのベースブランチからでも作成でき、 lich がそのワークツリーで新しいセッションを開きます。 ## プロバイダー対応状況 どのエージェントも、実際のターミナルで動き、会話を再開でき、サンドボックスで隔離でき、 ほかのセッションにも届きます。違うのは、lich がセッションから何を*読み取れる*かです。 各 CLI が記録する情報がそれぞれ異なるためです。

どの「なし」もすべて意図したもので、それぞれの裏にある計測結果は [`docs/ceilings.md`](docs/ceilings.md) にまとめています。 ## 設定 - **プロバイダー**：設定 › プロバイダーで、各エージェントのバイナリと全プロジェクト共通の既定を 設定します。プロジェクトごとに別のものを選ぶこともできます。パスを設定していない場合、 lich はログインシェルの `PATH` で最初に見つかったバイナリを実行し、 複数のバージョンがあると `lich doctor` が警告します。 - **フッター**：設定 › 外観で、項目をドラッグして表示する内容を決めます。 費用はトークン単位で課金される場合にしか意味のない数値なので、初期状態では非表示です。 - **ワークツリー**：プロジェクトに置いた `.worktreeinclude` ファイルで、 gitignore 対象のファイルのうちどれを新しいワークツリーにコピーするかを選べます。 - **セッションフック**：設定から [lich プラグイン](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich-plugin)を インストールすると、セッションが自分のカードに名前を付け、 ファイルを書き込んだ時点で git の状態が更新されるようになります。 - **スクリプト連携**：lich のどの部分をスクリプトから使っても安全かは、 [docs/stability.md](docs/stability.md) にまとめています。 ## プライバシーと更新 すべて手元のマシン上で動きます。アカウントもサインインもテレメトリもありません。 lich が自分からネットワークに接続するのは、次の場合だけです。 - **更新**：起動時と以後1時間ごとに、GitHub Releases で新しいバージョンを確認します。 起動時には、lich プラグインのリリース一覧も取得します。 - **プランの使用量**：各プロバイダーの使用量エンドポイント（Anthropic、OpenAI、Cursor、 OpenCode Go）に、エージェントがすでに使っているログインで問い合わせます。頻度は多くても5分に1回です。 Antigravity のプランは `agy` から直接読み取ります。 - **価格**：同梱の価格表にないモデルがあると、GitHub 上の LiteLLM の公開価格表を一度だけ取得します。 Windows インストーラー版はその場で更新されます。Homebrew、Scoop、AUR、 Linux のパッケージでインストールした場合はそれぞれのパッケージマネージャーで更新し、 実行するコマンドは lich が表示します。 うまく動かないときは、`lich doctor` でセットアップを確認でき、`lich rage` はバグ報告用の情報を 1つのアーカイブにまとめます（どこにもアップロードしません）。 ログに何が含まれているか（パス、プロジェクト名とブランチ名、gh のログイン名。セッショントークンは含まれません）は、 添付する前に設定 › ヘルプで確認できます。バグ報告や機能要望は [Issues](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/issues) にお願いします。各バージョンの変更点は [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) にあります。 ## ソースからのビルド lich は2つのバイナリでできています。静的な純粋 Go のバックエンド `lich` と、 `native/` から cgo でビルドするウィンドウ `lich-native` です。必要なのは **Go 1.27.0 以降** と **[Task](https://taskfile.dev)** で、ウィンドウにはさらに C ツールチェーン、Gio のシステムパッケージ、 そして `native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT` に記されたコミットからビルドした `libghostty-vt` が必要です。 ビルド方法は [`native/slice.sh`](native/slice.sh)、ウィンドウの詳細は [`docs/native-window.md`](docs/native-window.md) にあります。 ```bash task build # バックエンドのバイナリ -> bin/lich task build:native # ウィンドウ -> bin/lich-native task run # ビルドして実行 task test # Go のテストスイート task package # .deb + .rpm + Arch .pkg.tar.zst を bin/ に出力（nfpm が必要） ``` エージェントを新しく1つ加えるのは、2つのリポジトリにまたがって十数個のファイルに手を入れる変更です。 どこを触るかは [`docs/adding-a-provider.md`](docs/adding-a-provider.md) にまとめています。 ## スポンサー lich は1人で開発・保守しています。スポンサーからの支援は開発に充てる時間をまかない、 プロジェクトの独立性を保つ助けになります。アプリに有料プランはなく、今後も作りません。 [**スポンサーになる**](https://github.com/sponsors/omartelo) ### 支援者 まだいません。 ## ライセンス [AGPL-3.0-only](LICENSE) © 2026 omartelo lich はフリーソフトウェアです。GNU Affero General Public License v3 の条件のもとで、 使用、研究、改変、再配布ができます。派生物を配布する場合やネットワーク経由で提供する場合は、 同じライセンスで公開する必要があります。v0.9.0 以前のリリースは引き続き MIT ライセンスです。

멀티 에이전트 ADE: 모든 에이전트를 동시에, 각자 자기 브랜치에서.
Claude Code, Codex, opencode 등 이미 쓰고 있는 에이전트를 각자 자기 worktree에서, 모두 한 창에서 실행하세요.

lich 다운로드 · lichdotdev.github.io/lich

## 주요 기능
### 에이전트를 나란히 세션을 분할 화면에 올려 두면 lich가 패널을 알아서 배치합니다. 어느 세션이 작업 중인지, 어느 세션이 내 응답을 기다리는지, 컨텍스트가 얼마나 남았는지 한눈에 보입니다.
### 설정 없이 작업마다 worktree 원하는 베이스에서 세션을 분기하면 lich가 `.env` 파일을 복사하고 비어 있는 개발 서버 포트를 배정합니다. 커밋하지 않은 작업도 함께 가져갈 수 있습니다.
### diff를 읽고, 줄마다 코멘트 에이전트가 바꾼 내용을 세션 옆에서 읽고, 손볼 줄에 코멘트를 달고, 모아 둔 코멘트를 프롬프트 하나로 세션에 돌려보냅니다.
### 페이지를 가리키고, 에이전트에게 말하기 에이전트는 세션 옆 탭에서 브라우저를 조작하고, 당신도 같은 페이지를 씁니다. 잘못된 곳을 가리켜 메모를 남기고, 모든 메모를 하나의 프롬프트로 돌려보내세요.
### 브라우저 없이 풀 리퀘스트 풀 리퀘스트를 열고, 그 브랜치의 에이전트에게 작성을 맡기고, 인라인으로 리뷰하고, 병합까지 한 창에서 끝냅니다.
### 내 취향대로 JSON으로 테마를 가져오거나 git 저장소에서 설치합니다. [문서 →](docs/themes.md)
그 밖에도: - **일을 넘기는 세션.** 한 에이전트가 다른 세션에 작업을 넘기고 답을 돌려받습니다. 셸에서도 `lich` 명령으로 똑같이 쓸 수 있습니다([문서](docs/cli.md)). - **샌드박스 에이전트.** 키, 자격 증명, 다른 저장소가 보이지 않는 샌드박스 안에서 에이전트가 권한 확인을 건너뛰도록 허용할 수 있습니다([한계](docs/ceilings.md)). - **개발 서버를 사이드바에.** 프로젝트에서 계속 띄워 두는 것을 저장해 두면 클릭 한 번으로 시작하고 멈출 수 있습니다. - **뭐든 바로 찾기.** `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K`로 세션 이름이나 세션에서 오간 내용으로 바로 이동합니다. - **내가 필요할 때 알림.** 세션이 내 응답을 기다리면 데스크톱 알림이 뜹니다. ## 설치 ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lichdotdev/lich/main/install.sh | sh ``` 한 줄이면 됩니다. 배포판을 감지하고 다운로드를 검증한 다음, 패키지 매니저로 lich를 설치합니다. | 플랫폼 | 설치 방법 | | --- | --- | | **Linux** | 위의 `install.sh` 또는 AUR [`lich-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/lich-bin) (`yay -S lich-bin`). `zenity`와 glibc 2.34 이상(Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9 이상)이 필요합니다. | | **macOS** | `brew install --cask lichdotdev/tap/lich` | | **Windows** | [Releases](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases)의 설치 프로그램이나 포터블 zip, 또는 `scoop install https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases/latest/download/lich.json` | macOS와 Windows 빌드는 아직 서명되지 않아, Releases에서 받은 파일에는 Gatekeeper와 SmartScreen이 경고를 띄웁니다. Homebrew로 설치하면 Gatekeeper 경고는 뜨지 않습니다. 배포판별 패키지, Linux tarball, quarantine 플래그 지우기, 예전 Homebrew formula에서 업그레이드하는 방법은 [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)에 있습니다. ## 시작하기 1. **프로젝트를 엽니다.** 탭 줄의 `+`를 누르면 최근에 닫은 항목이 나오고 폴더 선택기가 열립니다. 여기서 git 저장소를 고르세요. 2. **에이전트를 고릅니다.** 처음 실행하면 머신에서 찾은 에이전트 목록이 나옵니다. 설정 › 프로바이더에서 기본값과 바이너리 경로를 지정할 수 있습니다. 3. **세션을 시작합니다.** *새 세션*을 누르면 프로젝트에서 에이전트가 열립니다. 체크아웃 헤더의 `+`로는 원하는 에이전트나 일반 터미널을 바로 그 체크아웃에서 열 수 있습니다. 4. **worktree를 만듭니다** *(선택)*. 원하는 베이스 브랜치에서 하나 만들면 lich가 그 안에 새 세션을 열어 줍니다. ## 프로바이더 지원 모든 에이전트는 실제 터미널에서 실행되고, 대화를 재개할 수 있으며, 샌드박스 안에서 동작하고, 다른 세션에 접근할 수 있습니다. 에이전트마다 다른 것은 lich가 세션에서 *읽어 올* 수 있는 정보입니다. CLI마다 기록하는 내용이 다르기 때문입니다.

빈칸은 모두 의도된 것이며, 각각 무엇을 측정했는지는 [`docs/ceilings.md`](docs/ceilings.md)에 정리되어 있습니다. ## 설정 - **프로바이더.** 설정 › 프로바이더에서 에이전트별 바이너리 경로와 모든 프로젝트에 적용할 기본값을 지정하며, 프로젝트마다 따로 고를 수도 있습니다. 경로를 지정하지 않으면 lich는 로그인 셸의 `PATH`에서 가장 먼저 찾은 바이너리를 실행하고, 버전이 둘 이상이면 `lich doctor`가 경고합니다. - **하단 바.** 설정 › 모양에서 항목을 끌어다 놓아 무엇을 표시할지 정합니다. 비용은 토큰당 과금될 때만 의미가 있으므로 처음에는 숨겨져 있습니다. - **worktree.** 프로젝트의 `.worktreeinclude` 파일로 gitignore된 파일 중 어느 것을 새 worktree에 복사할지 정합니다. - **세션 훅.** 설정에서 [lich 플러그인](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich-plugin)을 설치하면 세션이 자기 카드의 제목을 직접 정하고, 파일을 쓰는 즉시 git 상태를 새로 고칩니다. - **스크립팅.** lich에서 스크립트로 안심하고 다뤄도 되는 부분은 [docs/stability.md](docs/stability.md)에 정리되어 있습니다. ## 개인 정보와 업데이트 모든 것이 내 머신에서 실행됩니다. 계정도, 로그인도, 텔레메트리도 없습니다. lich가 네트워크에 접속하는 경우는 아래가 전부입니다. - **업데이트**: 시작할 때와 매시간 GitHub Releases에서 새 버전을 확인하고, 시작할 때 lich 플러그인의 릴리스 목록을 확인합니다. - **플랜 사용량**: 각 프로바이더의 사용량 엔드포인트(Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, OpenCode Go)에 에이전트가 이미 쓰고 있는 로그인 정보로 접속하며, 최대 5분에 한 번입니다. Antigravity의 플랜은 `agy`에서 직접 읽습니다. - **가격**: 번들된 가격표에 없는 모델이 있을 때 한 번, GitHub에 공개된 LiteLLM 가격표를 받아 옵니다. Windows 설치 프로그램으로 설치한 빌드는 lich가 직접 업데이트합니다. Homebrew, Scoop, AUR, Linux 패키지로 설치했다면 해당 패키지 매니저로 업데이트하며, 실행할 명령은 lich가 알려 줍니다. 문제가 생겼다면 `lich doctor`가 설정을 점검하고, `lich rage`는 아무것도 업로드하지 않고 버그 리포트를 아카이브 하나로 모아 줍니다. 로그 파일을 첨부하기 전에 설정 › 도움말에서 로그에 무엇이 담기는지(경로, 프로젝트와 브랜치 이름, gh 로그인 계정이며 세션 토큰은 절대 담기지 않음) 확인할 수 있습니다. 버그와 기능 요청은 [이슈](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/issues)에 남겨 주세요. 버전별 변경 사항은 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)에서 볼 수 있습니다. ## 소스에서 빌드 lich는 바이너리 두 개로 이루어집니다. 백엔드 `lich`는 정적 순수 Go 바이너리이고, 창 `lich-native`는 `native/`에서 cgo로 빌드합니다. 필요한 것은 **Go 1.27.0+**와 **[Task](https://taskfile.dev)**이며, 창을 빌드하려면 C 툴체인과 Gio의 시스템 패키지, 그리고 `native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT`에 적힌 커밋에서 빌드한 `libghostty-vt`가 추가로 필요합니다. 빌드 방법은 [`native/slice.sh`](native/slice.sh)에, 창에 대한 설명은 [`docs/native-window.md`](docs/native-window.md)에 있습니다. ```bash task build # 백엔드 바이너리 -> bin/lich task build:native # 창 -> bin/lich-native task run # 빌드 + 실행 task test # Go 테스트 스위트 task package # bin/에 .deb + .rpm + Arch .pkg.tar.zst (nfpm 필요) ``` 에이전트를 하나 더 추가하려면 두 저장소에 걸쳐 파일 십여 개를 고쳐야 합니다. 어디를 고쳐야 하는지는 [`docs/adding-a-provider.md`](docs/adding-a-provider.md)에 정리되어 있습니다. ## 후원 lich는 한 사람이 만들고 유지 관리합니다. 후원금은 프로젝트에 들이는 시간을 뒷받침하고 프로젝트가 독립성을 지키게 해 줍니다. 앱에 유료 요금제는 없으며 앞으로도 생기지 않습니다. The multi-agent ADE: all your agents working at once, each on its own branch.
Claude Code, Codex, opencode or the agent you already use, each in its own worktree, all in one window.

Download lich · lichdotdev.github.io/lich

## Features
### Agents side by side Put sessions on a wall and lich lays out the panes for you. See at a glance which one is busy, which one is waiting on you and how much context it has left.
### A worktree per task, no setup Branch a session off any base and lich copies your `.env` files and gives it a free dev-server port. Your uncommitted work can come along.
### Review the diff, comment the lines Read what the agent changed next to its session, comment on the lines that need work and send every note back as one prompt.
### Point at the page, tell the agent The agent drives a browser in a tab beside its session, and you use the same page. Point at what's wrong, leave a note on it and send every note back as one prompt.
### Pull requests without the browser Open a pull request, ask the branch's agent to write it, review it inline and merge it, all from the same window.
### Make it yours Import a theme as JSON or install one from a git repository. [Docs →](docs/themes.md)
And also: - **Sessions that delegate.** One agent hands a task to another session and gets the answer back. The same works from your shell with the `lich` command ([docs](docs/cli.md)). - **Sandboxed agents.** Let an agent skip permission prompts inside a sandbox that can't see your keys, your credentials or your other repositories ([limits](docs/ceilings.md)). - **Your dev servers in the sidebar.** Save what a project keeps running and start or stop it with one click. - **Find anything.** `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K` jumps to a session by name or by something said in it. - **Know when you're needed.** A desktop notification when a session is waiting on you. ## Install ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lichdotdev/lich/main/install.sh | sh ``` One line: it detects your distro, checks the download and installs lich with your package manager. | Platform | Get it | | --- | --- | | **Linux** | `install.sh` above, or AUR [`lich-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/lich-bin) (`yay -S lich-bin`). Needs `zenity` and glibc 2.34 or newer (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9 and up). | | **macOS** | `brew install --cask lichdotdev/tap/lich` | | **Windows** | Installer or portable zip from [Releases](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases), or `scoop install https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases/latest/download/lich.json` | The macOS and Windows builds are not signed yet, so Gatekeeper and SmartScreen warn on a download from Releases; Homebrew skips the Gatekeeper prompt. Per-distro packages, the Linux tarball, clearing the quarantine flag and upgrading from the old Homebrew formula are in [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). ## Getting started 1. **Open a project.** The `+` in the tab strip lists what you closed recently and opens a folder picker. Point it at a git repository. 2. **Pick your agent.** The first launch lists the agents it found on your machine. Settings › Providers sets the default and each binary's path. 3. **Start a session.** *New Session* opens your agent in the project. The `+` on a checkout's header opens any agent, or a plain terminal, in that checkout. 4. **Give it a worktree** *(optional)*. Create one from any base branch and lich opens a fresh session in it. ## Provider support Every agent runs in a real terminal, resumes its conversation, works in the sandbox and reaches your other sessions. What changes from one to another is what lich can read back out of it, since each CLI records different things.

Every gap is deliberate, and [`docs/ceilings.md`](docs/ceilings.md) says what was measured behind each one. ## Configuration - **Providers.** Settings › Providers sets each agent's binary and the default for every project; a project can choose its own. With no path set, lich runs the first binary on your login shell's `PATH` and `lich doctor` warns when there is more than one version. - **Footer.** Settings › Appearance: drag its items to choose what it shows. The cost starts hidden, since it only means something when you pay per token. - **Worktrees.** A `.worktreeinclude` file in the project picks which gitignored files a new worktree gets. - **Session hooks.** Install the [lich plugin](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich-plugin) from Settings and a session names its own card and refreshes git the moment it writes a file. - **Scripting.** [docs/stability.md](docs/stability.md) says which parts of lich are safe to script against. ## Privacy & updates Everything runs on your machine: no account, no sign-in, no telemetry. lich only goes to the network for: - **Updates**: a version check against GitHub Releases at startup and hourly, and the lich plugin's release list at startup. - **Plan usage**: each provider's own usage endpoint (Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, OpenCode Go), with the login the agent already uses, at most every five minutes. Antigravity's plan is read from `agy` itself. - **Prices**: LiteLLM's public price table on GitHub, once, for a model the bundled table does not know. The Windows installer updates in place; Homebrew, Scoop, AUR and the Linux packages update through their package manager, and lich gives you the command. Something broken? `lich doctor` checks your setup and `lich rage` packs a bug report into one archive without uploading it. Settings › Help says what the log carries (paths, project and branch names, your gh login, never a session token) before you attach it. Bugs and feature requests go to [Issues](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/issues); what changed in each version is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Build from source lich is two binaries: `lich`, a static pure-Go backend, and `lich-native`, the window, built with cgo from `native/`. You need **Go 1.27.0+** and **[Task](https://taskfile.dev)**; the window also needs a C toolchain, Gio's system packages and a `libghostty-vt` built from the commit in `native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT`. [`native/slice.sh`](native/slice.sh) says how, and [`docs/native-window.md`](docs/native-window.md) covers the window. ```bash task build # backend binary -> bin/lich task build:native # window -> bin/lich-native task run # build + run task test # Go suites task package # .deb + .rpm + Arch .pkg.tar.zst in bin/ (needs nfpm) ``` Adding another agent touches a dozen files across two repositories: [`docs/adding-a-provider.md`](docs/adding-a-provider.md) is the map. ## Sponsors lich is written and maintained by one person. Sponsoring pays for the time that goes into it and keeps the project independent: there is no paid tier of the app and there will not be one. Claude Code, Codex, opencode ou o agente que você já usa, cada um na própria worktree, todos na mesma janela.

Baixar o lich · lichdotdev.github.io/lich

## Recursos
### Agentes lado a lado Coloque as sessões num split e o lich arruma os painéis sozinho. Veja de relance quem está trabalhando, quem está esperando por você e quanto contexto ainda resta.
### Uma worktree por tarefa, sem configurar nada Crie uma sessão a partir de qualquer branch e o lich copia seus arquivos `.env` e reserva uma porta livre para o servidor de desenvolvimento. O que você ainda não commitou pode ir junto.
### Revise o diff e comente as linhas Leia o que o agente mudou ao lado da sessão dele, comente as linhas que precisam de ajuste e mande todas as notas de volta num único prompt.
### Aponte na página, fale com o agente O agente pilota um navegador numa aba ao lado da sessão, e você usa a mesma página. Aponte o que está errado, deixe uma nota em cima e mande todas as notas de volta num prompt só.
### Pull requests sem abrir o navegador Peça ao agente da branch para abrir o pull request, revise linha a linha e faça o merge, tudo na mesma janela.
### Do seu jeito Importe um tema em JSON ou instale um direto de um repositório git. [Docs →](docs/themes.md)
E mais: - **Sessões que delegam.** Um agente passa uma tarefa para outra sessão e recebe a resposta de volta. O mesmo funciona do seu shell com o comando `lich` ([docs](docs/cli.md)). - **Agentes em sandbox.** Deixe um agente pular os pedidos de permissão dentro de uma sandbox que não enxerga suas chaves, suas credenciais nem seus outros repositórios ([limites](docs/ceilings.md)). - **Seus servidores de desenvolvimento na barra lateral.** Salve o que o projeto mantém rodando e ligue ou desligue com um clique. - **Ache qualquer coisa.** `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K` pula para uma sessão pelo nome ou por algo que foi dito nela. - **Saiba quando precisam de você.** Notificação no desktop quando uma sessão está esperando por você. ## Instalação ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lichdotdev/lich/main/install.sh | sh ``` Um comando só: ele detecta a sua distro, confere o download e instala o lich pelo gerenciador de pacotes. | Plataforma | Como instalar | | --- | --- | | **Linux** | O `install.sh` acima, ou o AUR [`lich-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/lich-bin) (`yay -S lich-bin`). Precisa do `zenity` e da glibc 2.34 ou mais nova (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9 em diante). | | **macOS** | `brew install --cask lichdotdev/tap/lich` | | **Windows** | Instalador ou zip portátil em [Releases](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases), ou `scoop install https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases/latest/download/lich.json` | Os builds de macOS e Windows ainda não são assinados, então o Gatekeeper e o SmartScreen avisam num download pela página de Releases; pelo Homebrew, o aviso do Gatekeeper não aparece. Pacotes por distro, o tarball para Linux, como tirar a flag de quarentena e como atualizar a partir da fórmula antiga do Homebrew estão no [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). ## Primeiros passos 1. **Abra um projeto.** O `+` na barra de abas lista o que você fechou recentemente e abre o seletor de pastas. Escolha um repositório git. 2. **Escolha o seu agente.** Na primeira execução, o lich lista os agentes que encontrou na máquina. Em Configurações › Provedores você define o padrão e o caminho de cada binário. 3. **Inicie uma sessão.** *Nova sessão* abre o seu agente no projeto. O `+` no cabeçalho de um checkout abre qualquer agente, ou um terminal comum, naquele checkout. 4. **Dê uma worktree para ela** *(opcional)*. Crie uma a partir de qualquer branch base e o lich abre uma sessão nova nela. ## Suporte por provedor Todo agente roda num terminal de verdade, retoma a conversa, funciona na sandbox e fala com as suas outras sessões. O que muda de um para outro é o que o lich consegue ler de volta, porque cada CLI registra coisas diferentes.

Toda lacuna é proposital, e o [`docs/ceilings.md`](docs/ceilings.md) diz o que foi medido em cada uma. ## Configuração - **Provedores.** Em Configurações › Provedores você define o binário de cada agente e o padrão de todos os projetos; um projeto pode escolher o dele. Sem caminho definido, o lich roda o primeiro binário do `PATH` do seu shell de login, e o `lich doctor` avisa quando há mais de uma versão. - **Rodapé.** Em Configurações › Aparência, arraste os itens para escolher o que ele mostra. O custo começa oculto, porque só faz sentido se você paga por token. - **Worktrees.** Um arquivo `.worktreeinclude` no projeto escolhe quais arquivos ignorados pelo git vão para cada worktree nova. - **Hooks de sessão.** Instale o [plugin do lich](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich-plugin) pelas Configurações e a sessão dá nome ao próprio card e atualiza o git assim que grava um arquivo. - **Scripts.** O [docs/stability.md](docs/stability.md) diz quais partes do lich são seguras para usar em scripts. ## Privacidade e atualizações Tudo roda na sua máquina: sem conta, sem login, sem telemetria. O lich só acessa a rede para: - **Atualizações**: verificação de versão no GitHub Releases ao iniciar e a cada hora, e a lista de releases do plugin do lich ao iniciar. - **Uso do plano**: o endpoint de uso de cada provedor (Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, OpenCode Go), com o login que o agente já usa, no máximo a cada cinco minutos. O plano do Antigravity é lido do próprio `agy`. - **Preços**: a tabela pública de preços do LiteLLM no GitHub, uma vez, quando a tabela embutida não conhece o modelo. O instalador do Windows se atualiza sozinho; Homebrew, Scoop, AUR e os pacotes Linux atualizam pelo gerenciador de pacotes, e o lich mostra o comando. Algo quebrou? O `lich doctor` confere a sua instalação e o `lich rage` junta um bug report num único arquivo, sem enviar nada. Configurações › Ajuda mostra o que vai no log (caminhos, nomes de projeto e de branch, seu login do gh, nunca um token de sessão) antes de você anexá-lo. Bugs e pedidos vão nas [Issues](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/issues); o que mudou em cada versão está no [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Compilar a partir do código-fonte O lich são dois binários: o `lich`, um backend estático em Go puro, e o `lich-native`, a janela, compilada com cgo a partir de `native/`. Você precisa de **Go 1.27.0+** e do **[Task](https://taskfile.dev)**; a janela pede também um toolchain C, os pacotes de sistema do Gio e uma `libghostty-vt` compilada a partir do commit em `native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT`. O [`native/slice.sh`](native/slice.sh) explica como, e o [`docs/native-window.md`](docs/native-window.md) descreve a janela. ```bash task build # binário do backend -> bin/lich task build:native # janela -> bin/lich-native task run # compila + roda task test # suítes Go task package # .deb + .rpm + Arch .pkg.tar.zst em bin/ (precisa do nfpm) ``` Adicionar outro agente mexe em uma dúzia de arquivos de dois repositórios, e o mapa está em [`docs/adding-a-provider.md`](docs/adding-a-provider.md). ## Patrocinadores O lich é escrito e mantido por uma pessoa só. O patrocínio paga o tempo investido nele e mantém o projeto independente: o app não tem plano pago e não vai ter. Мультиагентная ADE: все ваши ИИ-агенты работают одновременно, каждый в своей ветке.
Claude Code, Codex, opencode или тот агент, которым вы уже пользуетесь: у каждого свой worktree, и всё в одном окне.

## Возможности
### Агенты бок о бок Выведите сессии на один экран, и lich сам разложит панели. С первого взгляда видно, какая сессия занята, какая ждёт вас и сколько контекста у неё осталось.
### Worktree под каждую задачу, без настройки Создайте сессию от любой базовой ветки, и lich скопирует ваши `.env`-файлы и выделит ей свободный порт для dev-сервера. Незакоммиченные изменения можно взять с собой.
### Читайте diff, комментируйте строки Смотрите, что изменил агент, рядом с его сессией, комментируйте строки, которые нужно доработать, и отправляйте все заметки назад одним промптом.
### Укажите на странице, скажите агенту Агент управляет браузером во вкладке рядом со своей сессией, а вы пользуетесь той же страницей. Укажите, что не так, оставьте на этом заметку и отправьте все заметки обратно одним промптом.
### Pull request'ы без браузера Откройте pull request, попросите агента ветки написать его, прочитайте прямо в коде и смёржите, не выходя из того же окна.
### Настройте под себя Импортируйте тему как JSON или установите её из git-репозитория. [Документация →](docs/themes.md)
А ещё: - **Сессии, которые делегируют.** Один агент передаёт задачу другой сессии и получает ответ обратно. То же работает из вашей оболочки через команду `lich` ([документация](docs/cli.md)). - **Агенты в песочнице.** Позвольте агенту пропускать запросы разрешений внутри песочницы, где не видны ваши ключи, учётные данные и остальные репозитории ([ограничения](docs/ceilings.md)). - **Ваши dev-серверы в боковой панели.** Сохраните то, что проект держит запущенным, и запускайте или останавливайте это одним щелчком. - **Поиск по всему.** `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+`K` открывает сессию по имени или по тому, что в ней обсуждалось. - **Знайте, когда вы нужны.** Уведомление на рабочем столе, когда сессия ждёт вас. ## Установка ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lichdotdev/lich/main/install.sh | sh ``` Одна строка: она определит ваш дистрибутив, проверит загрузку и установит lich через ваш пакетный менеджер. | Платформа | Где взять | | --- | --- | | **Linux** | `install.sh` выше или AUR [`lich-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/lich-bin) (`yay -S lich-bin`). Нужны `zenity` и glibc 2.34 или новее (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04, RHEL 9 и новее). | | **macOS** | `brew install --cask lichdotdev/tap/lich` | | **Windows** | Установщик или portable zip со страницы [Releases](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases) либо `scoop install https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/releases/latest/download/lich.json` | Сборки для macOS и Windows пока не подписаны, поэтому Gatekeeper и SmartScreen предупреждают о файле, скачанном со страницы Releases; при установке через Homebrew запроса Gatekeeper нет. Пакеты под отдельные дистрибутивы, tarball для Linux, снятие флага карантина и переход со старой формулы Homebrew описаны в [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). ## Быстрый старт 1. **Откройте проект.** Кнопка `+` на панели вкладок показывает недавно закрытые проекты и открывает диалог выбора папки. Выберите git-репозиторий. 2. **Выберите агента.** При первом запуске lich покажет агентов, которых нашёл на вашей машине. В разделе Настройки › Провайдеры задаются агент по умолчанию и путь к исполняемому файлу каждого. 3. **Запустите сессию.** Кнопка *Новая сессия* открывает вашего агента в проекте. Кнопка `+` в заголовке checkout открывает любого агента или обычный терминал именно в этом checkout. 4. **Создайте worktree** *(по желанию)* от любой базовой ветки: lich откроет в нём новую сессию. ## Поддержка провайдеров Каждый агент работает в настоящем терминале, возобновляет свой разговор, работает в песочнице и добирается до ваших остальных сессий. Отличается то, что lich может прочитать из сессии, потому что каждый CLI записывает своё.

Все пробелы намеренные: что именно измерялось за каждым из них, описано в [`docs/ceilings.md`](docs/ceilings.md). ## Настройка - **Провайдеры.** В разделе Настройки › Провайдеры задаются путь к исполняемому файлу каждого агента и агент по умолчанию для всех проектов; проект может выбрать свой. Если путь не задан, lich запускает первый исполняемый файл из `PATH` вашей login-оболочки, а `lich doctor` предупреждает, если версий несколько. - **Нижняя панель.** В разделе Настройки › Оформление перетаскиванием элементов выбирается, что она показывает. Стоимость по умолчанию скрыта, потому что эта цифра имеет смысл, только если вы платите за токены. - **Worktree.** Файл `.worktreeinclude` в проекте задаёт, какие файлы, игнорируемые git, попадут в новый worktree. - **Хуки сессии.** Установите [плагин lich](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich-plugin) из настроек, и сессия сама даст название своей карточке и обновит статус git сразу, как только запишет файл. - **Скрипты.** В [docs/stability.md](docs/stability.md) сказано, какие части lich можно спокойно использовать в скриптах. ## Конфиденциальность и обновления Всё работает на вашей машине: ни аккаунта, ни входа, ни телеметрии. lich выходит в сеть только за следующим: - **Обновления**: проверка версии в GitHub Releases при запуске и раз в час, а также список релизов плагина lich при запуске. - **Лимиты подписки**: собственный эндпоинт каждого провайдера с данными об использовании (Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, OpenCode Go), с тем логином, который уже использует агент, не чаще раза в пять минут. Подписку Antigravity lich узнаёт у самого `agy`. - **Цены**: публичная таблица цен LiteLLM на GitHub, один раз для модели, которой нет во встроенной таблице. Версия из установщика для Windows обновляется на месте; установки через Homebrew, Scoop, AUR или пакет Linux обновляются своим пакетным менеджером, и lich подскажет нужную команду. Что-то сломалось? `lich doctor` проверит вашу настройку, а `lich rage` соберёт отчёт об ошибке в один архив и ничего никуда не загрузит. Раздел Настройки › Справка ещё до того, как вы приложите файл журнала, показывает, что в нём есть: пути, названия проектов и веток, ваш логин gh, но никогда не токен сессии. Об ошибках и с пожеланиями пишите в [Issues](https://github.com/lichdotdev/lich/issues), а что изменилось в каждой версии, смотрите в [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## Сборка из исходников lich состоит из двух бинарников: `lich`, статический бэкенд на чистом Go, и `lich-native`, окно, которое собирается с cgo из `native/`. Понадобятся **Go 1.27.0+** и **[Task](https://taskfile.dev)**; для окна нужны ещё компилятор C, системные пакеты Gio и `libghostty-vt`, собранная из коммита, указанного в `native/GHOSTTY_COMMIT`. Как её собрать, описано в [`native/slice.sh`](native/slice.sh), а само окно в [`docs/native-window.md`](docs/native-window.md). ```bash task build # бинарник бэкенда -> bin/lich task build:native # окно -> bin/lich-native task run # сборка + запуск task test # тесты Go task package # .deb + .rpm + Arch .pkg.tar.zst in bin/ (нужен nfpm) ``` Добавление ещё одного агента затрагивает дюжину файлов в двух репозиториях: карта всех мест: [`docs/adding-a-provider.md`](docs/adding-a-provider.md). ## Спонсоры lich пишет и поддерживает один человек. Спонсорство оплачивает время, которое уходит на проект, и сохраняет его независимость: платной версии приложения нет и не будет.
