O lich o distingue do opencode 1 pela versão e o abre do jeito que o 2 espera: cada sessão num servidor próprio, de modo que o perfil, o modelo e as ferramentas do lich chegam a ele, com forks, Expandir pastes longos, logins de perfil e o medidor do OpenCode Go funcionando como no opencode 1. As conversas iniciadas no opencode 2, e as do opencode 1 que ele continuou, voltam a mostrar custo, últimas palavras e resultados de busca, e aparecem no Histórico. O spinner, o anel, o sino e o título do card precisam da próxima versão do plugin do lich, instalada em Configurações › Provedores, que agora vai para onde o opencode 2 lê plugins e toma o lugar da cópia que um lich mais antigo instalou. Uma sessão aberta pelo lich não fica no servidor compartilhado em segundo plano do opencode 2, então `opencode pair` e o app desktop não a enxergam.
- O título Descrição da Visão geral na tela de Pull requests tem um menu ⋯, como os comentários do GitHub: Copiar link copia o endereço do pull request, Copiar Markdown copia a descrição como foi escrita, e Editar abre a descrição para edição, o que antes o botão Editar ao lado do título fazia.
- Um agente pode gerenciar os serviços de um projeto como o rodapé de Serviços faz: listar, criar, editar, excluir, iniciar, parar, forçar a parada e reiniciar um serviço, iniciar ou parar todos, e ler o que um serviço imprimiu, rodando ou parado, com as ferramentas MCP `*_service` ou com `lich service` num terminal. Um serviço é nomeado pelo nome dele no projeto, o do próprio agente, a menos que ele cite outro.

### Changed

- No seu próprio pull request, a tela de Pull requests não oferece mais Aprovar nem Pedir alterações, que o GitHub recusa ao autor, e o menu do diff não oferece mais um comentário no pull request. O menu do diff também deixa de fora Comentar no pull request quando nenhuma linha está selecionada, em vez de mostrá-lo desativado como antes.
- As descrições, os comentários e as prévias de Markdown de pull request ficaram mais fáceis de ler, com texto mais claro, títulos e links mais nítidos, código em linha destacado, mais espaço entre linhas e blocos, e itens de lista quebrados alinhados com o texto deles.
- A tela de Pull requests abre num índice dos pull requests do projeto ocupando a tela inteira, e um pull request abre no lugar dele em vez de ao lado da lista. Um botão de voltar sobre o título retorna ao índice como você o deixou; ao lado dele, o número abre um menu dos outros pull requests, e anterior e próximo percorrem o filtro do índice. Na aba Arquivos só a árvore de arquivos fica ao lado do diff, que ganha a largura que a lista ocupava. A Visão geral põe a descrição ao lado de uma coluna com os revisores, as verificações, a possibilidade de merge e o checkout em que a branch está; a faixa de abas termina com o tamanho do pull request. Abrir em sessão e Merge ficam no cabeçalho, com Resolver conflitos ou Corrigir erros de CI ao lado quando o pull request precisa de um, e Aprovar, Atualizar e Abrir no GitHub passam para o menu ⋯. A tela se alinha ao espaçamento da barra lateral, seus botões têm o tamanho dos do resto da janela, e o código de que uma thread de revisão trata fica num bloco próprio, separado dos comentários. No índice, j e k ou as setas movem, Enter abre e / vai para o filtro; num pull request, Esc volta e Alt com uma seta passa ao pull request anterior ou ao próximo.
- O tema Dark que acompanha o lich dá à interface e ao terminal o mesmo fundo carvão neutro, eliminando o tom azul-escuro do terminal, e usa uma paleta de terminal e de sintaxe mais viva, de verde, coral, âmbar, azul, violeta e ciano. O tema Light usa versões mais escuras dessas cores, ajustadas para o contraste no fundo claro do terminal.
- O navegador de uma sessão não é mais fechado sem perguntar. Quando nenhum painel o mostra e ninguém o usa há cinco minutos, um toast pergunta se deve fechá-lo: Fechar o fecha, e Manter aberto, ou dispensar o toast com um deslize, o mantém por mais cinco minutos. Sem resposta, o toast fica na tela e o navegador fica aberto, então uma página deixada aberta durante o almoço continua lá quando você volta. Usar o navegador, ou o agente usá-lo, tira o toast da tela. Antes, o navegador era fechado após cinco minutos longe da sessão dele, e a página, as abas e o login se perdiam.
- Na tela de Pull requests, o botão que envia as threads de revisão abertas de um pull request para a sessão dele fica no cabeçalho ao lado de Abrir em sessão, em todas as abas, do tamanho dos botões ao redor. Antes era um botão pequeno no topo da aba Conversa, fora de vista quando a conversa rolava.
- A faixa de redimensionamento da barra lateral fica na própria borda direita dela, como a do painel Código e Revisão, em vez de no vão entre a barra lateral e as sessões.
- A barra lateral é uma árvore de sessões. Uma sessão é uma linha: o anel dela, o nome, o pull request e as alterações, e um canto onde um … sob o ponteiro abre o menu da sessão, com fechar incluído. O que as outras linhas do card diziam foi para o tooltip dele: a ferramenta que o turno roda ou o que ele espera, há quanto tempo, o caminho e o modelo. Cada checkout é uma linha própria, com a branch, o pull request e as alterações, e as sessões dele pendem dela. Uma sessão aberta por outra (um fork, uma sessão aberta com `open_session` ou `lich open`, um card de subagente) pende da sessão que a abriu, mesmo rodando em outra worktree, e uma mãe recolhe os filhos, mantendo a contagem e a marca de aguardando ou não lida. As linhas se movem pela sua linha: quando uma mãe se abre, uma sessão abre ou uma worktree ou uma pasta aparece, uma linha se abre já com o nome nela e a linha desce até ela e desenha o anel; recolher ou fechar tira o nome, apaga o anel e sobe a linha de volta, e a saída da última sessão de uma worktree ou de uma pasta leva a linha da worktree, ou a pasta, embora depois dela. Uma pasta fica numa bandeja, então se vê onde ela termina. Fixar foi para o menu do card, que também copia o comando `lich reply` de um pedido que a sessão deve. Um projeto sem worktree mantém uma lista plana. A barra lateral recolhida mostra a mesma árvore numa coluna: o nó de cada checkout, a linha passando por suas sessões, o anel menor de um filho na linha da mãe, e cada pasta na sua bandeja, com as linhas entrando e saindo pela mesma linha. Arrastar uma sessão solta a linha dela, mostra um espaço tracejado onde ela vai se juntar à árvore e desenha a linha de volta até ela quando pousa; a pasta ou worktree em que ela seria arquivada acende inteira. Uma mãe arrastada leva os filhos com ela, e uma sessão só pousa onde a árvore a mantém, nunca entre uma mãe e seu filho. Uma sessão arquivada numa pasta que tem cor assume essa cor, então a pasta a mantém, seja arrastando a sessão para lá, escolhendo a pasta no menu dela, ou um agente arquivando com `file_session` ou `lich file`; uma sessão aberta numa pasta, o worker de um subagente ou a sessão que o pediu também a usa. Soltar uma sessão numa pasta mais abaixo na barra lateral a arquiva de novo, onde antes ela voltava ao seu lugar quando uma worktree acima também a recebia. A barra lateral recolhida também arrasta sessões, e o botão de busca dela abre o mesmo filtro da barra aberta, que continua filtrando o trilho depois que o painel fecha.
- Na Visão geral da tela de Pull requests, o título Descrição e o ⋯ dele ficam no lugar no topo da coluna enquanto a descrição rola por baixo, sobre um separador, e o ⋯ fica na borda direita da coluna.
- Os placeholders de carregamento da tela de Pull requests combinam com o que carrega no lugar deles: o índice mostra linhas da altura das reais, com a coluna de verificações onde ela cai, preenchendo a tela, e um pull request mostra a linha do título com seus botões, a faixa de abas real e o layout da aba aberta (a descrição ao lado dos fatos, os commits, as verificações, os avatares e comentários da conversa, ou a barra de ferramentas, a árvore e os cards dos arquivos), em vez de algumas barras genéricas. A conversa e o diff mostram os mesmos placeholders enquanto carregam, no lugar de uma linha de texto.

### Fixed

- Uma revisão, resposta ou outra ação de pull request que o GitHub recusa diz o motivo, como uma revisão pendente deixada aberta no github.com ou um comentário numa linha fora do diff. Antes, toda recusa dizia "gh could not complete the request", porque o motivo enviado pelo GitHub era descartado.
- Um comentário de revisão pendente sob a sua linha na aba Arquivos da tela de Pull requests tem Editar e Descartar, como na aba Conversa. Antes, só podia ser alterado ou descartado pela aba Conversa.
- Na aba Arquivos da tela de Pull requests, expandir as linhas escondidas entre as alterações, visualizar um arquivo Markdown e mostrar uma imagem funcionam num pull request cuja branch não está em checkout em lugar nenhum. Eles falhavam com "Couldn't read" o arquivo, porque o lich o procurava numa pasta com o nome do endereço do pull request.
- A aba de um pull request na tela de Pull requests abre no topo. Antes, abria onde a aba ou o pull request anterior tinha sido rolado, então a aba Conversa podia abrir no fim.
- O código citado numa thread de revisão na tela de Pull requests mostra a indentação em vez de uma caixa para cada tab.
- Um campo de arquivo no navegador da sessão, como o envio de uma foto de perfil, abre o seletor de arquivos do sistema ao clicar, e aceita vários arquivos quando o campo permite. Antes, o clique não fazia nada.
- Sair de uma página do navegador da sessão que pergunta antes de você ir não recarrega mais a página no lugar numa máquina ocupada; o navegador vai para onde estava indo.
- Um agente que clica num ponto do navegador da sessão não erra mais o ponto depois que você move o lich para outro monitor, redimensiona o painel do navegador ou muda o zoom dele. As capturas de tela dele agora estão nos mesmos pixels que os cliques, que um monitor HiDPI ou um zoom de página tinham deixado até 1,5 vez maiores, e um clique num ponto lido de uma captura tirada antes de o painel mudar de tamanho é recusado, dizendo ao agente para tirar uma nova.
- O lich não mantém mais a GPU ocupada enquanto uma sessão trabalha. O spinner de uma aba de projeto redesenhava a janela inteira na taxa de atualização do monitor, e com sessões ocupadas em mais de um projeto o lich segurava mais da metade da GPU de um notebook, tirando-a dos jogos e de tudo o mais. Todo spinner, o anel de ocupado da barra lateral e a pulsação de um serviço em execução agora redesenham no máximo 24 vezes por segundo, e 8 vezes por segundo enquanto a janela do lich não está em foco, então o anel de uma sessão ainda é visto girando de outro monitor. O ponto de um serviço em execução pulsa a cada seis segundos em vez de a cada dois e meio: cada pulso é uma rajada de quadros, e o ritmo antigo eram oito quadros por segundo o dia inteiro para um ponto.
- Enquanto uma sessão trabalha, a janela desenha 24 quadros por segundo, a taxa do cinema, em vez de 30, e a saída do terminal da sessão é desenhada no próximo quadro do anel de ocupado em vez de pedir quadros próprios: um agente transmitindo e um anel girando custam uma taxa de quadros, não a soma das duas. O que você digita continua aparecendo no instante em que o terminal ecoa.
- O terminal não redesenha mais a linha do cursor a cada quadro enquanto o cursor fica parado; a linha é recomposta quando o cursor se move ou o texto dela muda.
- No Linux, a janela desenha só o que mudou desde o último quadro e informa essa área ao compositor, em vez de repintar tudo 24 vezes por segundo enquanto uma sessão trabalha: um quadro em que só o anel de ocupado girou desenha o anel e a linha do cursor do terminal, e o trabalho da placa de vídeo no renderizador da janela cai para um quinze avos. O Windows e o macOS continuam desenhando quadros inteiros. `GIO_DAMAGE=off` no ambiente desenha quadros inteiros também no Linux, para um driver gráfico que informa errado o que seus buffers guardam.
- A janela do lich usa metade do processador que usava enquanto uma sessão trabalha. Todo ícone, anel e arco na tela era reconstruído a partir do contorno a cada quadro; agora cada um é construído uma vez e mantido na placa de vídeo.

  eles: ali guardam o login no Keychain ou em uma pasta que nenhuma configuração
  consegue mover, então todo perfil compartilharia uma só conta.

### Changed

- **Toda atualização abre a janela nativa.** A primeira execução de cada versão
  muda o lich para a janela nativa, recorrendo à web onde ela não consegue
  iniciar; volte nas Configurações e o lich fica na janela web até a próxima
  versão. Na primeira vez que a janela nativa abre, ela diz que é experimental e
  leva a um relato de bug.
- **Um anel de status mais leve na janela nativa.** O anel em volta do ícone do
  card de uma sessão é desenhado mais fino, para ter o peso que a janela web lhe
  dá.

- **Teclas de atalho mais folgadas na janela nativa.** As teclas na paleta de
  comandos, na janela de atalhos e em Configurações › Atalhos têm mais espaço em
  volta do texto, que fica centralizado.

- **As Configurações da janela nativa abrem em Global.** A engrenagem na barra
  superior sempre abre as Configurações em Global, em vez do escopo em que você
  as deixou por último; a aba de um projeto continua abrindo as configurações
  dele em Configurações do projeto….

- **Uma paleta de comandos mais calma na janela nativa.** Cada sessão, projeto e
  mensagem ocupa uma linha, com o caminho depois do nome; o caminho de uma
  worktree mostra as suas três últimas partes. As sessões que esperam por você
  vêm primeiro e dizem isso, e as abas de filtro trocam as pílulas por um
  sublinhado. Uma sessão fechada no Histórico mostra a branch e a idade à
  direita, e uma segunda linha só quando uma busca encontrou a conversa dela,
  com as palavras marcadas.

### Fixed

- **Uma sessão reiniciada não aparece mais como ocupada para sempre.** Uma sessão
  cujo agente morreu no meio de um turno, ou que foi fechada no meio de um turno,
  voltava no mesmo card ainda listada como ocupada para as outras sessões: uma
  tarefa enviada a ela esperava por um turno que nunca terminaria. Agora ela
  começa sem estado, como uma nova.
- **Codex, Cursor CLI, Antigravity e Crush deixam de perguntar o que você já
  respondeu.** Uma sessão em sandbox de qualquer um deles abre direto no prompt.
  O Cursor CLI e o Antigravity não perguntam mais de novo em uma worktree de uma
  pasta em que você confiou, nem o Antigravity nas subpastas dela, e o Crush não
  pede mais para inicializar cada nova worktree. Uma sessão do oh-my-pi em
  sandbox não abre mais no assistente de configuração.
- **O Claude Code deixa de perguntar "confiar nesta pasta?" onde você já
  respondeu.** Uma pasta em que você confiou na sua conta principal passa a ser
  confiável em todos os outros perfis do Claude Code a partir da próxima sessão
  ali, e uma sessão do Claude Code em sandbox abre sem a pergunta. Uma sessão que
  o lich abriu para você não fica mais parada nessa tela, onde Enter sai.
- **Uma janela nativa reaberta sabe para onde cada sessão foi.** Uma sessão que
  tinha se movido com `cd`, ou para dentro do tmux ou do ssh, voltava mostrando o
  caminho, a branch e as alterações do checkout dela até o próximo `cd`; agora a
  janela lê onde cada uma esteve por último ao se conectar.
- **A janela nativa escreve os prompts dos agentes no idioma dos seus prompts.**
  Os handoffs de pull request e de issue e um lote de comentários de revisão
  eram sempre digitados em inglês.
- **Trocar o tema durante uma reconexão não derruba mais a janela nativa.**
  Trocar o tema, ou o sistema alternar entre claro e escuro, enquanto a janela se
  reconectava a um lich reiniciado podia pintar terminais que a reconexão tinha
  acabado de liberar e derrubar a janela.
- **Texto em chinês, japonês e coreano não congela mais a janela nativa no
  Linux.** Uma sessão, uma Revisão ou um pull request cheio de texto CJK podia
  travar a janela por segundos, o bastante para o "não está respondendo", e um
  zoom trazia o congelamento de volta.
- **A janela nativa usa menos memória.** O terminal de cada sessão e a Revisão
  carregavam a própria cópia das fontes de reserva, dezenas de megabytes cada
  uma para uma fonte CJK ou de emoji: seis sessões abertas agora ocupam cerca da
  metade da memória de antes. Ela também inicia mais rápido em uma máquina com
  fontes CJK instaladas.
- **Reabrir uma sessão cuja conversa já está aberta foca esse card.** Uma sessão
  fechada vinda do Histórico, um fechamento desfeito ou uma worktree existente
  podiam voltar como um segundo card em uma conversa que outro card ainda
  rodava, e os dois escreviam no mesmo transcript. O Histórico lista essa
  conversa uma só vez, pelo fechamento mais recente, e Esquecer remove todas as
  cópias dela.

Беседы, начатые в opencode 2, и беседы opencode 1, которые он продолжил, снова показывают стоимость, заключительные слова и результаты поиска и перечислены в «Истории». Сервис задаётся его именем в проекте, по умолчанию это сервис самого агента, если он не назвал другой.

### Changed

- Боковая панель — это дерево сессий. Сессия занимает одну строку: кольцо, имя, pull request и изменения, и уголок, где … под указателем открывает меню сессии, в том числе «Закрыть». То, что говорили остальные строки карточки, перенесено в её подсказку: инструмент, который выполняет ход, или то, чего он ждёт, как долго, путь и модель. Каждая рабочая копия — отдельная строка со своей веткой, pull request и изменениями, и её сессии свисают с неё. Сессия, которую открыла другая (форк, сессия, открытая через `open_session` или `lich open`, карточка субагента), висит на открывшей её сессии, даже если работает в другой worktree, а родительская сессия сворачивает своих потомков, сохраняя счётчик и отметку ожидания или непрочитанного.   каждый CJK- или эмодзи-шрифт: шесть открытых сессий теперь занимают примерно
  вдвое меньше памяти. На машине с установленными CJK-шрифтами оно ещё и
  стартует быстрее.
- **Повторное открытие сессии, чей разговор уже открыт, переходит на эту
  карточку.** Закрытая сессия из «Истории», отменённое закрытие или
  существующий worktree могли вернуться второй карточкой на разговоре, который
  другая карточка ещё вела, и обе писали в один транскрипт. «История» теперь
  показывает такой разговор один раз, по последнему закрытию, а «Забыть»
  удаляет все его копии.

## [0.84.0] - 2026-11-03

### Added

- 拉取请求界面中，拉取请求的“对话”标签页会在每位作者的评审和评论旁显示其 GitHub 头像，排成左侧的一列，和 GitHub 一样。评审讨论串内的评论，无论在“对话”标签页还是“文件”标签页，之间都用一条线隔开。头像加载完成之前，或账号没有头像时，会显示作者的首字母。
- 拉取请求描述和评论中的任务列表，会显示一个已勾选或未勾选的复选框，而不是字面上的 `[x]` 或 `[ ]`。
- 拉取请求描述和评论中的一级标题，会像 GitHub 那样在文本的整个宽度上加下划线。
- lich 插件的主题技能用于编写、移植或修复 lich 颜色主题，现在以 `lich-theme` 之名也送达 opencode、oh-my-pi、Crush 和 Kiro CLI；此前只有 Claude Code、Codex、Antigravity 和 Cursor CLI 有。在 opencode 中它是 `/lich-theme` 命令。在下次从设置 › 提供商安装或更新插件时生效。
- lich 现在可以运行 opencode 2。lich 通过版本号区分它和 opencode 1，并按 2 期望的方式启动它：每个会话在各自的服务器上，因此它的配置档案、模型和 lich 的工具都能送达，分叉、展开长粘贴、配置档案登录和 OpenCode Go 仪表的表现都和 opencode 1 一样。在 opencode 2 中开始的对话，以及 opencode 1 的对话被它继续后，会重新显示成本、收尾内容和搜索结果，并列在历史中。卡片的旋转指示、圆环、提示铃和标题需要 lich 插件的下一个版本，从设置 › 提供商安装；它现在会安装到 opencode 2 读取插件的位置，并取代旧版 lich 安装的副本。lich 打开的会话不在 opencode 2 共享的后台服务器上，因此 `opencode pair` 和桌面应用看不到它。
- 拉取请求界面“概览”中的“描述”标题有了 ⋯ 菜单，和 GitHub 的评论一样：“复制链接”复制拉取请求的地址，“复制 Markdown”复制描述的原文，“编辑”打开描述进行编辑，这原来由标题旁的“编辑”按钮完成。
- 代理可以像“服务”页脚那样管理项目的服务：列出、创建、编辑、删除、启动、停止、强制停止和重启某个服务，一次启动或停止全部服务，并读取某个服务（运行中或已停止）输出的内容，方式是用 `*_service` MCP 工具，或在终端中使用 `lich service`。服务以它在项目中的名称指定，除非另行指定，否则是代理自己的项目。

### Changed

- 在你自己的拉取请求上，拉取请求界面不再提供“批准”或“请求更改”，GitHub 不允许作者这样做；差异的菜单也不再提供对拉取请求的评论。未选中任何行时，差异的菜单也不再显示置灰的“对拉取请求的评论”，而是直接省略。
- 拉取请求的描述、评论和 Markdown 预览更易阅读：文字更亮，标题和链接更清晰，行内代码高亮，行与块之间留有更多空间，折行的列表项与其文本对齐。
- 拉取请求界面现在以横跨整个界面的项目拉取请求索引打开，拉取请求在原处打开，而不是在列表旁边。标题上方的返回按钮会回到你离开时的索引；旁边的编号会打开其他拉取请求的菜单，上一个和下一个则沿着索引的筛选依次浏览。在“文件”标签页中，差异旁边只有文件树，差异因此获得了列表原先占用的宽度。“概览”把描述放在一列旁边，这一列包含评审者、检查、可合并性以及分支所在的检出目录；标签栏末尾显示拉取请求的大小。“在会话中打开”和“合并”留在标题栏，拉取请求需要时，旁边还有“解决冲突”或“修复 CI 错误”，而“批准”、“刷新”和“在 GitHub 上打开”移到 ⋯ 菜单。该界面与侧边栏的间距对齐，按钮与窗口其余部分的大小一致，评审讨论串所指的代码放在单独的块中，与评论分开。在索引上，j 和 k 或方向键移动，Enter 打开，/ 转到筛选；在拉取请求上，Escape 返回，Alt 加方向键切换到上一个或下一个。
- 内置的深色主题让界面和终端使用相同的中性炭灰背景，去掉了终端的蓝黑色调，并使用更明亮的终端和语法调色板，包括绿色、珊瑚红、琥珀色、蓝色、紫罗兰色和青色。浅色主题使用这些颜色更深的对应色，针对浅色终端背景的对比度做了调整。
- 会话的浏览器不再不经询问就被关闭。当没有窗格显示它，并且五分钟内没人使用时，会弹出提示询问是否关闭：“关闭”会关闭它，“保持打开”或将提示滑走，则让它再保留五分钟。不回应时，提示会一直显示，浏览器也保持打开，因此午饭时留着的页面回来时仍在。使用浏览器，或代理使用它，会让提示消失。此前，离开会话五分钟后浏览器就会关闭，页面、标签页和登录状态都会丢失。
- 在拉取请求界面，把拉取请求未解决的评审讨论串发送给其会话的按钮，现在位于标题栏“在会话中打开”旁边，在每个标签页上都有，大小与周围的按钮一致。此前它是“对话”标签页顶部的一个小按钮，对话滚动后就看不到了。
- 侧边栏的调整大小条位于侧边栏自己的右边缘，和代码与评审面板的一样，而不是位于侧边栏与会话之间的空隙中。
- 侧边栏现在是会话树。一个会话占一行：它的圆环、名称、拉取请求和更改，以及一个角落，指针下的 … 会打开会话的菜单，其中包括关闭。卡片其他行原来显示的内容移到了它的提示中：这一轮正在运行的工具或在等待的内容、已持续的时间、路径和模型。每个检出目录单独占一行，带有它的分支、拉取请求和更改，它的会话挂在其下。由另一个会话打开的会话（分叉、用 `open_session` 或 `lich open` 打开的会话、子代理卡片）挂在打开它的会话下，即使它运行在另一个 worktree 中；母会话可以把子会话折叠起来，保留数量以及等待或未读标记。各行沿着连线移动：母会话展开、会话打开，或 worktree 或文件夹出现时，一行带着名称展开，连线向下延伸到它并画出它的圆环；折叠或关闭时，名称消失、圆环擦除，连线向上收回，而一个 worktree 或文件夹的最后一个会话离开时，worktree 的行或文件夹也随之消失。文件夹位于托盘上，因此它在哪里结束一目了然。置顶移到了卡片的菜单中，菜单还能复制会话所欠请求的 `lich reply` 命令。没有 worktree 的项目保持扁平列表。折叠后的侧边栏用一列显示同一棵树：每个检出目录的节点、贯穿其会话的连线、母会话连线上子会话较小的圆环，以及托盘上的每个文件夹，其各行沿同一条连线进出。拖动会话时它会脱离自己的连线，显示一个虚线槽位，标出它将加入树的位置，落下后连线再画回它；它将被归入的文件夹或 worktree 会整体亮起。被拖动的母会话会带着它的子会话，会话只会落在树允许的位置，绝不会落在母会话和它的子会话之间。归入带颜色的文件夹的会话会采用该颜色，使文件夹保留它，无论你把它拖到那里、在其菜单中选择该文件夹，还是由代理用 `file_session` 或 `lich file` 归入；在文件夹中打开的会话、子代理的工作会话或请求它的会话也会带上该颜色。把会话拖到侧边栏更下方的文件夹上会再次归档它，此前当上方的 worktree 也接纳它时，它会回到原来的位置。折叠后的侧边栏也可以拖动会话，它的搜索按钮会打开与展开的侧边栏相同的筛选，面板关闭后筛选仍会继续作用于侧边栏的窄栏。
- 在拉取请求界面的“概览”中，“描述”标题及其 ⋯ 在描述于其下滚动时，留在这一列的顶部，下方有一条分隔线，⋯ 位于这一列的右边缘。
- 拉取请求界面的加载占位符与在它们位置加载出的内容一致：索引显示与真实行同高的行，检查列位于实际所在位置，并铺满整个界面；拉取请求显示带按钮的标题行、真实的标签栏，以及打开的标签页的布局（描述及其旁边的信息、提交、检查、对话的头像和评论，或文件的工具栏、树和卡片），而不是几条通用的条形。对话和差异在加载时显示同样的占位符，而不是一行文字。

### Fixed

- GitHub 拒绝的评审、回复或其他拉取请求操作，现在会说明原因，例如 github.com 上遗留了未提交的待处理评审，或评论所在的行不在差异中。此前每次拒绝都显示“gh could not complete the request”，因为 GitHub 发送的原因被丢弃了。
- 拉取请求界面“文件”标签页中，某行下方的待处理评审评论有了“编辑”和“丢弃”，和“对话”标签页一样。此前只能在“对话”标签页中修改或丢弃它。
- 在拉取请求界面的“文件”标签页中，展开更改之间隐藏的行、预览 Markdown 文件和显示图像，现在对分支没有在任何地方检出的拉取请求也有效。此前它们会以“Couldn't read”该文件而失败，因为 lich 在一个以拉取请求地址命名的文件夹中查找它。
- 拉取请求界面中，拉取请求的标签页现在从顶部打开。此前它会停在上一个标签页或拉取请求滚动到的位置，因此“对话”标签页可能在末尾打开。
- 拉取请求界面评审讨论串中引用的代码，现在显示其缩进，而不是每个制表符显示成一个方框。
- 会话浏览器中的文件输入（例如上传头像）在点击时会打开系统的文件选择器，输入允许时可选择多个文件。此前点击没有任何反应。
- 在会话浏览器中，对一个离开前会询问的页面选择“离开”，在繁忙的机器上不再改为重新加载该页面；浏览器会前往原本要去的地方。
- 把 lich 移到另一个显示器、调整浏览器窗格大小或更改其缩放之后，代理在会话浏览器中点击某个点不再偏离。它的截图现在与点击使用相同的像素，HiDPI 显示器或页面缩放此前使截图最多大了 1.5 倍；而按窗格改变大小之前截取的截图读取的点位进行点击，会被拒绝，并告诉代理重新截一张图。
- 会话工作时，lich 不再让 GPU 保持忙碌。项目标签页的旋转指示以显示器的刷新率重绘整个窗口，当不止一个项目中的会话在忙时，lich 占用了笔记本一半以上的 GPU，使游戏和其他一切都得不到它。现在每个旋转指示、侧边栏的忙碌圆环和运行中服务的跳动，每秒最多重绘 24 次，在 lich 窗口没有焦点时每秒 8 次，因此在另一个显示器上仍能看到会话的圆环在转。运行中服务的圆点每六秒跳动一次，而不是每两秒半一次：每次跳动都是一阵帧，而旧的节奏意味着一个圆点全天每秒八帧。
- 会话工作时，窗口每秒绘制 24 帧（电影的帧率），而不是 30 帧，并且会话终端的输出在忙碌圆环的下一帧绘制，而不是自己再请求帧：流式输出的代理和旋转的圆环只占一个帧率，而不是两者之和。你输入的内容仍会在终端回显的那一刻显示。
- 光标停在原处时，终端不再在每一帧都重绘光标所在的行；只有光标移动或该行文本变化时才会重新合成该行。
- 在 Linux 上，窗口只绘制自上一帧以来变化的部分，并告知合成器该区域，而不是在会话工作时每秒重绘全部内容 24 次：只有忙碌圆环转动的帧，只绘制圆环和终端的光标行，窗口渲染器中显卡的工作量降到十五分之一。Windows 和 macOS 仍绘制完整帧。在环境中设置 `GIO_DAMAGE=off`，在 Linux 上也会绘制完整帧，适用于误报其缓冲区内容的显卡驱动。
- 会话工作时，lich 窗口使用的处理器减少了一半。屏幕上的每个图标、圆环和圆弧，此前每一帧都从轮廓重新构建；现在每个只构建一次，并保存在显卡上。

## [0.83.0] - 2026-10-29

# Adding a provider

A **provider** is an agent CLI lich can run inside a session's PTY. There are
eight (`internal/providers.Registry`), and adding a ninth means landing in
about a dozen files across two repositories. This is the map — written after
Antigravity, so it names what that change actually touched rather than what it
should have. Cursor CLI came later and needed no plugin install at all — it runs
every Claude Code hook on the machine, which is a shape the plugin table below
does not have; [`providers/cursor.md`](providers/cursor.md) carries what that
buys and what it costs.

Two rules govern the whole exercise, and both are in
[`../CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md):

- **Every table here is read off that CLI's own `--help` or a real run.** A flag
  guessed from a sibling is a spawn that dies before the session exists, and an
  event name copied from another harness is a report that silently never fires.
  Nothing below is inferred from a provider's documentation alone. Read the
  `--help` of the command lich actually spawns: a CLI with subcommands has one
  parser per level, and a flag that exists under one is rejected by the other.
  Kiro CLI is the worked example — `--agent` and `--resume-id` are its root's,
  `--model` and `--trust-all-tools` its `chat` subcommand's, so lich spawns
  `kiro-cli chat` and `subcommandArgs` puts that word first.
- **A gap is allowed; a silent one is not.** Equal behaviour across providers is
  often impossible. Where the new provider cannot do something the others can,
  the same PR adds a [`ceilings.md`](ceilings.md) bullet naming what is out and
  why.

## Measure first

Before editing anything, get these answers from the real binary. Every one of
them is a row in a table below, and a wrong answer is invisible until a user
hits it.

| Question | How it was answered for Antigravity |
|---|---|
| What is the binary called? | `agy` — the name on `PATH`, not the product's |
| Which page documents installing that CLI? | The install instructions, not the product's front door — and `curl -sI` it before it lands |
| How does it resume a conversation by id? | `--conversation <id>` (`--help`) |
| How does it skip permission prompts? | `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (`--help`) |
| How is it told which model to run? | `--model <name>` (`--help`) |
| How is it told a reasoning effort? | `--effort <level>` (`--help`) |
| Can it append to its system prompt at spawn? | No — its whole flag list has nothing for it |
| Can it be handed an MCP server on its command line? | No — MCP lives behind `agy mcp add` |
| Where are its credentials, config and conversations? | `~/.gemini` (+ `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/`), found by running it against a throwaway `HOME` |
| What proves a conversation still exists? | `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations/<id>.db` |
| What are its lifecycle events, and what is on their payloads? | A real run with a hook that dumps stdin: `PreInvocation`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostInvocation`, `Stop`, all camelCase |
| How is a plugin installed, and does its CLI install a *release*? | `agy plugin install` takes a directory and clones only a default branch — so lich writes the released files itself |

The rig for the last two is the cheap part and the one worth keeping: point the
binary at a throwaway `HOME`, register a hook that writes its stdin to a file,
and run one short non-interactive turn. That is how the payload field names, the
working directory a hook command runs in, the absence of any `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`
and the fact that a hook printing `{}` **denies** the tool call were all
established for Antigravity — none of which is in its docs, and the last two
would each have shipped as a plugin that silently does nothing or breaks every
tool.

## The backend

| File | What it holds | What a new provider adds |
|---|---|---|
| `internal/providers/providers.go` | the registry | an id constant, a `Registry` entry (id, display name, binary names, install-docs URL), a line in `AcceptsMCPServer` if it takes an MCP server at spawn, and one in `SupportsFork` — that one is a table every provider must appear in, so a new id fails its test until it is answered, plus an arm in `CostSourceOf` if it records spend |
| `internal/terminal/command.go` | what a spawn runs | entries in `skipPermissionFlags`, `modelFlags`, `effortFlags`, `briefingFlags` and `resumeArgs` (with a fork arm there if the CLI branches a conversation) — each one optional, and absent means "no flag rather than somebody else's" — plus a `subcommandArgs` arm if the session is a subcommand rather than the bare binary, and an `mcpArgs` arm (or, for one told through its environment, an `mcpEnv` one) if it is in `AcceptsMCPServer` |
| `internal/terminal/resume.go` | whether a resume can be offered | a `ResumeAvailable` case answering from what that provider left on disk |
| `internal/terminal/transcript.go`, `sessiondb.go` | where that state lives | the path resolver the case above calls |
| `internal/terminal/usage.go` | the footer's session readout | a `usageSourceFor` arm, plus a `sessionCost` arm reading whatever that provider records about spend — and a `contextUsageFor` arm only if it also records the model's context window. Which rung that lands the provider on is a row in `docs/ceilings.md`, in the same PR |
| `internal/terminal/said.go`, `search.go`, `index.go` | the recap beside a diff, the palette's Messages tab and the conversation a parked session is indexed with | an arm in `transcriptReaderFor` with a line reader for a provider that files its conversation as JSONL, or the `said` and `search` queries in `sessiondb.go` for one that keeps it in a database of its own — a provider in neither is simply never listed, which is what every other miss in those searches looks like. All three readers go through the same two arms, so a provider that lands here is searchable in the History tab too |
| `internal/terminal/startgate.go` | when a session can take typed work | an entry in `startsAtPrompt` only if its hook reports session-start from the agent's own prompt before the first turn, past any trust question; that report is then what makes its sessions ready for work. Measure it in a fresh worktree |
| `internal/terminal/conversations.go`, `conversations_stores.go` | conversations started outside lich (the History tab's Outside lich group) | a `conversationReaders` entry listing that provider's stored conversations; absent means they are never offered |
| `internal/quota/` | plan usage in Settings and the footer | a `<provider>.go` reader and its place in `Service.read`, only if the provider exposes plan limits; a gap is a `docs/ceilings.md` line |
| `internal/sandbox/sandbox.go` | what a confined session can still reach | a `stateDirs` case — a provider missing here confines to a home with no credentials, which is a session that opens and cannot log in |
| `internal/agentplugin/` | the companion plugin | a `<provider>.go` with install / installed-version, plus the two switches (`Install`, `installedVersion`), `registersServerAtInstall` and the `supported` list in `agentplugin.go`, and a `registrations` entry in `repair.go` if the install writes an MCP server |
| `internal/cli/mcp.go` | the `open_session` tool schema | the new id in the `kind` description |

Nothing else in the backend enumerates providers: the settings store keys
everything on the id (`provider.<id>.bin`, `.enabled`, `.sandbox`,
`.skip-permissions`), and `providers.Known` guards ids arriving from outside.

## The native window

| File | What a new provider adds |
|---|---|
| `native/cmd/lich-native/providericon.go` | the id in `providerIcons`, with a Lobe mark or a Lucide fallback. Its keys are every kind the window knows (`providerKinds`), so a provider absent here is absent from every per-provider list in Settings |
| `native/cmd/lich-native/spawn_gate.go` | the id in `resumableKinds` if its CLI reopens a conversation |
| `native/cmd/lich-native/fork.go` | the id in `forkableKinds` if its CLI branches a conversation |
| `native/cmd/lich-native/settings_providers.go` | its `skipFlags` spelling (the switch in Settings is hidden for a provider absent here, which is what stops the UI promising a flag the spawn has none for), and a `loginCommands` entry only if `internal/quota` reads a plan for it |
| `native/cmd/lich-native/toolline.go` | a rule only if it spells MCP tool names in a shape not already handled |
| `native/cmd/lich-native/footer_handson.go` | a rung in `handsOnRung`: whether the hands-on clock hears that provider through a turn its hooks open, or only through its tool calls. No compiler checks it, and a provider missing from it reads as a turn one |
| `native/backend/store.go` | nothing: `DetectedProvider` is `api`'s, so a JSON tag moves in `api/providers.go` and in `api/testdata/contract.golden` |

`Registry.Docs` is the one field with a check outside the compiler: it is what the
"Not found on PATH" row and the no-agents dialog link to, so a blank or dead one
turns the screen a user without that agent meets back into the dead end the field
exists to close. Verify it against the live web before landing it —
`curl -sI -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n' <url>` — follow every
redirect to the final address, and record the date you checked in the commit body.
`TestEveryProviderDocumentsItsInstall` fails on an empty one; nothing but that
curl catches a page that has moved.

The two `skipPermissionFlags` tables — Go and TypeScript — are the one place a
provider is spelled twice on purpose. Both are pinned in tests as literals
rather than read from each other: this is the flag that hands an agent the
machine, and a test that follows the map cannot see the map hand a provider
somebody else's flag.

## The plugin

The companion repository (`lichdotdev/lich-plugin`) owns the client side of every
[hook contract](hooks/README.md), and lich cannot see it break. Move the
contract first — the tables in `docs/hooks/` — then both sides.

What a harness needs from the plugin is one of two shapes, decided by the
harness and not by lich:

- **It runs commands.** Then it gets a hook-registration file mapping its own
  event names onto the scripts already in `hooks/`, and the install is either
  its plugin CLI (Claude Code, Codex) or lich writing the files (Antigravity,
  Crush, Kiro CLI).
- **It loads a module.** Then it gets a single-file client of its own
  (`opencode/lich.js`, `omp/lich.js`) posting the same payloads to the same
  endpoints.

Register only the reports that harness can actually close. A `busy` with no
end-of-turn event behind it pins a spinner to the card until the next turn — a
state that is wrong for longer than it is right, which is why Crush registers
two of the four reports and not four.

**The fixtures are the handshake, and lich moves first.**
[`docs/hooks/fixtures/`](hooks/fixtures/) is every contract as bytes, and the
plugin's suite asserts against the same lines. A provider id lich has not
registered is rejected by `/session-start` — so until the line below lands here,
the plugin cannot carry a fixture for it, and its own tests name the gap in a
`PENDING_UPSTREAM` set that fails once the fixture lands — which is the signal
to empty it:

```json
{"name":"antigravity conversation id","body":{"session_id":"s1","provider_session_id":"…","provider":"antigravity"}, "accept":{…}}
```

The id in that line is the one the plugin passes its report script
(`report-session-start.sh antigravity`). They have to be the same string, and
nothing but a session wearing the wrong icon says so when they are not.

## The paperwork

Not optional, and all in the same PR:

- **`docs/hooks/*.md`** — a column per harness in each contract's mapping table,
  plus a paragraph for anything that harness does differently.
- **`docs/hooks/fixtures/session-start.jsonl`** — the accepted-provider line

## The gate

Beyond the [local gate](../CLAUDE.md), one thing is specific to this change: the
provider list is pinned in tests on both sides
(`TestStatusListsEveryHarness`, `TestDetect`, `isSessionKind`), and those
failures are the contract changing rather than a break. Update them naming which
one it is, and never the other way round.

# Decision: the session browser is a tab of frames

**Status: the card's Browser item opens it.** Right-click a session card →
**Browser**, above Open in. That opens a tab beside the session: its terminal
and its page, split as any layout is. The agent drives the same page through
`lich browser` and the `browser_*` MCP tools.

## Why frames and not a webview

lich's window is native (`docs/native-window.md`). On Linux it speaks Wayland
directly, without GTK, so no system webview fits inside it; Windows and macOS
would take one, Linux would not. The page is a **headless Chromium** on
`chromium.FindBrowser` (the system's Chrome, Edge, Chromium, Brave, Vivaldi
or Helium), with its own user-data directory. `browser.Attach` starts its
screencast at the pane's size; each frame reaches the window as
`browser:frame:<session>` and is acked only once sent, so a window slow to
draw slows the stream. The pane's pointer, keys, committed text (an input
method's or a paste) and toolbar go back through `browser.Mouse`, `.Key`,
`.Text` and `.Nav`, which light nothing up: only the agent's actions emit
`browser-agent`, which the pane shows as the agent chip and a mark where it
clicked.

## One browser per card

- the card's Browser item → its tab, starting a headless browser at
  `about:blank` when there is none. A session in another layout is asked
  about before it moves.
- the agent's `browser_open` first → a headless browser, and a toast in the
  bottom-right corner whose Open shows that same page in the tab
- **Open in a window** → the page reopens as a headed window on the same
  profile, with its cookies (session ones included); its tab goes. chromedp
  cannot show a headless process in place, so what lives only in the page, a
  half-filled form or sessionStorage, does not survive. Browser on the card
  then brings that window forward.

`browser-state` tells the window when a browser starts, closes, moves to a
window or loads another page; `browser.Running` is what a window reads when
it attaches. A browser no pane shows and no one used for five minutes is
never closed on its own: its state turns `idle`, the window asks with a toast,
and Close (`browser.Close`) or Keep open (`browser.Keep`, five more minutes)
answers. Unanswered, it stays open and is not asked about again; any use
withdraws the question. One a pane shows, or a window, is never asked about.
The tab takes no other
session, and closing its page closes the browser.

## What the agent may load

`http`, `https`, `about:blank`. Not `file:`, `javascript:`, `data:`, `chrome:`.
A local file inside the session's checkout, typed or sent as an absolute path
or a `file:` URL, loads over http instead (`internal/preview`): the backend
serves that checkout on `127.0.0.1`, at its `LICH_WORKTREE_PORT` plus 1000, so
each checkout is its own origin, and a path outside the checkout is refused.
Page info never includes form values. Screenshots are files. Click, type and
press are real input events. `press` is named keys only. Arbitrary JavaScript
in the page is not a tool.

## Notes on the page

The crosshair on the pane's toolbar stops the pointer reaching the page: the
element under it is outlined, the outline sliding to the next element in 160
ms as the pointer moves, and a click opens a note on it. Notes wait in a
tray floating over the bottom of the page, which never resizes for it, each
element pinned where it stands, and Send types them into the session's prompt
as one message: each element's label, page, a
selector `browser_click` takes, its React component when the page is a
development build, its markup without any field's value, and the note. A note
opened from the tray or its pin scrolls its element into view first, unless it
already shows whole. An element inside a list, sidebar or dialog that scrolls
is outlined only where that box shows it, and one the box hides has no pin. The
page only answers what is where (`browser.ElementAt`, `browser.Locate`); the
outline, the pins and the note are the window's, so nothing is injected into
the page.

## Console errors

Each page answer (`browser_info`, `browser_click`, `browser_press`) names the
errors the page's console showed since the agent's last one, once each, as
`console error:` lines: a `console.error` call, an uncaught exception with
where it was thrown, or an error Chrome logs itself, such as a resource that
failed to load. Each is one line cut to 200 characters; past the first five, a
`(N more console errors)` line counts the rest. Warnings, info and log
messages are left out. The text is what the page logs, so a page that logs a
form's value hands it to the agent; lich reads nothing else.

## Dialogs

An `alert`, `confirm`, `prompt` or `beforeunload` the page opens stays open
until someone answers it, and until then the page runs no script and takes no
input. lich answers no dialog on its own:

- The pane shows it as a card over the top of the page, naming the site that
  opened it, with OK and Cancel (Leave and Stay for a `beforeunload`) and a
  field for a `prompt`. The person answers there.
- The agent's call that opened it answers at once, rather than hanging, with
  the page as it stood and a `dialog open:` line; any other call on that page
  fails with a message naming the dialog. `browser_dialog` (`lich browser
  dialog accept|dismiss`) answers it, and the pane plays the agent's cursor
  pressing the card's button. `text` is what a `prompt` returns on OK; left
  out, it returns its default text.
- Whichever answers first wins. A dialog the person answered reaches the
  agent's next page answer as a `dialog answered:` line.

Accepting a `beforeunload` less than a second after it opened waits out the
rest of that second: Chrome aborts the navigation it held when it is accepted
sooner, and reloads the page, which asks again. On a busy machine that second
can still be too soon; lich then takes the leave up again once the reload
lands, so Leave goes where it was going.

## File inputs

A click on a file input opens the system's file chooser, the one the footer's
attach button opens, for one file or several as the input asks; what the
person picks fills the input, and Cancel leaves it as it was. It opens only
while a pane shows the page: an agent's click on a file input in a page nobody
is looking at leaves it empty, and no tool fills one.

## Languages of the page answer

The line tags of a page answer (`url:`, `title:`, `wait:`, `text:`,
`interactive`, `downloaded:`, `downloading:`, `console error:`, `dialog
open:`, `dialog answered:`) stay English: the tool descriptions name them. The
prose around them, the element list's legend, the filled and checked marks,
the note that more elements wait below, and what a held dialog asks of the
agent, follows the session's prompt language.

## Downloads

A file the page downloads lands in the user's Downloads folder
(`XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR`, from the environment or `user-dirs.dirs`, on Linux;
`~/Downloads` elsewhere) under the name the page suggests, made unique the way
browsers do (`report (1).csv`): nothing already there is overwritten. Chrome
writes it under its download id into a staging folder inside the session's own
profile, and lich moves it to Downloads once it is complete; across
filesystems the move is a copy. What Chrome downloads on its own, with no page
announcing it, stays in staging and is deleted with the profile. A
click or key press that starts one answers with a `downloaded:` line, its path
and size, after waiting up to ten seconds for it; one still running answers
`downloading:`, and the next page read says when it ends. A file Chrome
finished but lich could not move into Downloads answers `download failed:`
with the path it would have taken. `browser_open` and
`browser_navigate` on a URL that answers with a file download it the same way:
Chrome aborts that navigation and the page stays where it was, so the answer
is the handle with `downloads` rather than an error. That answer also
waits until 2.5 seconds after the download began, because Chrome reloads the
page about 1.5 seconds after an `<a download>` and the reload aborts a
navigation started before it. `browser-download` tells the
window when a file is complete, and the window shows a toast naming it with a
button that opens its folder. The same holds in a window opened with Open in a
window.

## Tabs

The browser keeps a list of tabs and draws one, the front tab: a headless
Chrome draws no frames for a tab behind another. The pane's header shows the
pane's name and a + while there is one tab, and the tabs in its place once
there are more.

- What a tab opens in a new tab or window (`target=_blank`, `window.open`)
  joins the list right after it, in front when its opener was. Closing it,
  from the page's own `window.close()` or a ×, brings its opener back as it
  was, its script's state and login intact; a tab nobody opened gives way to
  the one beside it. The last tab cannot be closed.
- The + opens a blank tab in front with the address field focused.
- The agent lists them with `browser_tabs` (`lich browser tabs`), by index,
  and opens, selects or closes one with `browser_tab` (`lich browser tab new
  [url] | select <i> | close <i>`), which answers with the page then in front.
  Every other tool acts on the front tab. The pane plays the agent's cursor
  pressing the tab, its × or the +.
- A tab opened behind the front one shares its renderer when it keeps its
  opener, so a dialog there holds the front tab too: it reaches the pane and
  the agent at once, and the answer goes to the tab that opened it.

## Providers

Claude Code, Codex and opencode receive the tools at spawn. Antigravity,
oh-my-pi, Crush, Cursor CLI and Kiro receive them from the lich MCP server the
plugin registers. Downloads and dialogs reach all eight the same way: in the
answer of the same tools, and `browser_dialog` for all of them. Tabs too:
`browser_tabs` and `browser_tab` reach all eight.

# Known Ceilings

Deliberate limits and shortcuts, and the traps they set. A bullet earns its place by naming something that breaks
work when nobody knows it and that the call site never shows. The mechanism and the history stay in the code and
`CHANGELOG.md`; this file is the trap alone. Provider-specific behaviour is reference, not a trap, and lives in
[`providers/`](providers/).

## Spawn, start and resume

- **`LICH_WORKTREE_PORT` is reserved, never held** (`internal/terminal/worktreeport.go`): the number is a name the
  checkout owns, nothing binds it, and anything on the machine can take the port before the dev server starts.
- **A session is ready for work only once its agent reports from its own prompt, where it can**
  (`internal/terminal/startgate.go`): in a fresh worktree several providers ask a question first (trust the
  folder, initialize the project), and anything typed then (a relayed task, `lich open --prompt`, a scheduled
  prompt, an issue or pull request handed over) goes into the question, with the Enter behind it answering it
  (what each provider then does: `docs/providers/`, Spawn). Claude Code, Cursor CLI, oh-my-pi and Kiro CLI stay
  unready until their session-start report, which their hooks send only from the agent's prompt. That hold needs
  lich-plugin's hooks in the provider: without them nothing would ever release it, so nothing is held and the
  typed text lands in the question. Codex, Antigravity, Crush and opencode report nothing before their first
  turn, so a quiet screen is still all lich has for them.
- **opencode 2 is told apart by its `--version`, and every 2.x session runs a server of its own**
  (`internal/providers/version.go` `IsOpencode2`, `internal/terminal/opencode2.go`): 2.x keeps 1.x's binary name,
  config and database but not its argv, so the spawn asks the binary for its major, once per path, size and
  modification time. A wrapper whose `--version` answers for another opencode than the one it runs (a
  version-manager shim that picks one per directory) spawns with the other generation's argv, which dies on an
  unknown flag. A 2.x session runs `--standalone`, because the background service 2.x attaches to by default
  holds the environment of whichever command started it, which would leave a session without its profile, its
  model or lich's MCP server. The price is that a lich session is not on that service, so the user's other
  opencode clients (`opencode pair`, the desktop app) do not see it, and each one boots a server of its own. A
  fork goes through 2.x's own route (`POST /api/session/{id}/fork`, run before the spawn) because its terminal
  interface has no `--fork`; a fork that route refuses is refused, not reopened as a resume.
- **A reasoning effort is refused where the TUI would drop it, and never validated**
  (`internal/terminal/command.go`, `effortFlags`): `lich open --effort` and `open_session`'s `effort` are refused
  for opencode, Crush and Cursor CLI, whose interactive CLI takes no level, rather than handing back a session on
  its default (why each: `docs/providers/`, Spawn). The level itself is never validated,
  so a misspelled one is each provider's to handle, and most start without a word.
- **An ultracode turned off inside a Claude Code session comes back on its next restart**
  (`internal/terminal/command.go`, `ultracodeArgs`): Claude Code drops ultracode on `--resume`, so lich passes it
  on every spawn (`docs/providers/claude.md`, Spawn), and nothing turns it off for one session while the
  provider-wide switch is on.
- **A model or effort is a birth value, and some providers forget it on resume** (`internal/terminal/command.go`,
  `modelArgs`, `effortArgs`): lich passes neither when it resumes or forks a conversation, because a `/model` or
  `/effort` typed inside the session is the user's decision and re-sending the birth value would undo it. Claude
  Code's effort and all of Antigravity resume on the saved default rather than on the conversation's (each
  measurement in `docs/providers/`, Spawn), so a change made inside the session survives while a level or model
  lich set at birth falls back to that default. Cursor CLI also writes whatever model a spawn or resume runs on into
  `cli-config.json` as the default for every later `cursor-agent`, so `lich open --kind cursor --model` changes
  the user's Cursor default too.
- **Start new leaves the old conversation reachable only through History search**
  (`native/cmd/lich-native/exit_toast.go`): once the new conversation's session-start report arrives, the backend
  writes its id over the card's `provider_session_id`, and nothing on the card points back at the old one. Start
  new asks no confirmation for that reason.
- **A provider's "trust this folder?" answer is carried only where lich can find the person's own answer,
  and a confined session is told to skip the question** (`internal/claudeprofile/trust.go`,
  `internal/terminal/cursor_trust.go`, `antigravity_trust.go`, `crush_init.go`, `confinedEnv` and
  `confinedTrustArgs` in `internal/terminal/sandbox.go`; each provider in `docs/providers/`, Spawn and Sandbox):
  before a spawn into a worktree or a profile lich writes a provider's trust for the folder only when the person
  already trusted it in Personal or trusted its main checkout, and it never trusts a folder nobody trusted. A
  confined session skips the question, because what it guards against, a folder's own settings running on the
  machine, is what the sandbox confines; on Cursor CLI and Antigravity skipping it writes the trust down, so a
  folder once opened confined stays trusted outside the sandbox too. Whether Codex's trust and Cursor CLI's
  `--trust` loosen anything beyond the question was not measured.

## Session state and hooks

- **The sidebar's state chips read the ring, nothing more** (`native/cmd/lich-native/sidebar_filter.go`):
  Waiting, Running and Unread are the card's amber, spinning and unread green ring, and Idle is everything
  else, a read turn included. A provider that cannot raise a state cannot be filtered into it: Crush
  reports no turn at all and always sits under Idle; Antigravity, oh-my-pi, Kiro CLI and Cursor CLI raise no
  permission event, so they never reach Waiting (a Kiro or Cursor session blocked on a confirmation counts as
  Running).
  There is no error chip: no provider reports one, and a process that exited is known only to its terminal,
  not to a store the sidebar reads. The chips are not persisted, like the query.
- **Next waiting session reads the same ring** (`waitingTarget`, `native/cmd/lich-native/hotkeys_dispatch.go`):
  it jumps only to a card whose last report is Waiting, so it never lands on the five providers the chips above
  never put under Waiting. It walks the order next session walks,
  the cards the sidebar shows (`hotkeyCards`): a card in a folded block, under a folded mother, or left out by the
  search and state filter is skipped rather than unfolded, so a waiting session folded away is reached only through
  its block's mark. The active card never counts: when it is the only one waiting, the chord does nothing and
  goes on to the terminal.
- **An interrupted turn is read off the keystrokes, not from the provider** (`internal/terminal/draft.go`,
  `hookstate.go`, `Service.noteInterrupt`): Claude Code, Codex and oh-my-pi all skip the hook that ends a turn when
  the user stops one, so lich publishes `interrupted` itself when a lone Ctrl+C or Escape reaches a session it knows
  is mid-turn. It is also raised with no keystroke, when a Claude Code mod acks an abort sent from lich and when a
  usage limit ends a Codex turn (`internal/terminal/limit.go`). It is a guess made from bytes, and it has three
  edges. A provider session running a tool that owns the terminal — an editor opened through a shell command — takes
  Escape as the interrupt and clears the ring while the turn is still running; the next report from the provider
  puts it back. A provider that reports its own abort as the turn finishing wears the solid ring a completed turn
  does, because the provider's own word outranks the keystroke (opencode, `docs/providers/opencode.md`), and one
  that reports no state at all has no turn to end (Crush). And an errand the relay delivered survives an interrupt
  on purpose: stopping a turn is not answering the request, so the sender keeps waiting for the target's next turn
  rather than being told the work is over.
- **A finished turn is unread until its own card is watched** (`native/cmd/lich-native/cardstate.go`,
  `setFocused`): the solid emerald ring means "back from the agent, not read yet", and it
  fades only for the session whose terminal is on screen **while the window has focus**. A card left focused in a
  background window keeps its ring solid until the window is touched again, which is the point, but it also means
  a desktop that reports focus oddly never fades one.
- **Crush raises no hook at a turn's end, so nothing that waits for `done` fires there** (its only event is
  `PreToolUse`, 0.98.1; `docs/hooks/session-state.md`). A task handed to a Crush session that ends its turn
  without answering waits out its ticket (`internal/relay/observe.go`, `turnCandidates`): its database does mark
  the end (`finish.reason` other than `tool_use` in `.crush/crush.db`), but the conversation id reaches lich only
  on the first tool call, so a turn that calls no tool has nothing to read, and the asker hears nothing until the
  ticket's deadline. A pull request a Crush session opens reaches its card only when the window regains focus
  (`native/cmd/lich-native/gitstate.go` `recheckMissingPR`, `cardstate.go` `setFocused`): `gh pr create` moves
  neither branch nor HEAD, so a card showing no pull request asks gh again when its session's turn ends. A Crush
  card is never named after its conversation either: Crush files a title in that same database, and nothing tells
  lich when to read it (`docs/hooks/session-title.md`). The day Crush ships `Stop`, the existing
  `report-state.sh done` closes the first two, and a read like Kiro's and Cursor's (`internal/terminal`,
  `title_filed.go`) the third.
- **A CLI run as a tool inside a session is told apart by conversation id, and Kiro has none to tell by**
  (`internal/terminal/nested.go`, docs/hooks/session-state.md "Nested agent CLIs"): a `claude -p` the agent runs
  inherits the card's `LICH_*` env and reports as it. A state report naming another conversation is dropped, and a
  session-start naming one is dropped while the card's turn is open. A scripted Kiro CLI run (`--no-interactive`, how
  an agent runs one) carries no id in any hook payload (measured on 2.21.0), so a nested `kiro-cli` still reports
  as its host. The
  start guard reads lich's own turn, so a host lich never sees open cannot use it: a Crush session reports no turn
  at all, so a nested CLI's start can still move what its card resumes. A plugin older than 0.20 sends no id on state reports, which are then taken as
  before.
- **Keep-awake follows the session-state report, and only that** (`internal/awake`, `turnLog.onOpen`): the
  machine is held out of idle sleep while a hook says a turn is open, so what a provider reports decides whether
  the machine stays up at all (`docs/providers/`). Linux holds it through `systemd-inhibit --what=idle`: a distro
  without systemd logs one warning per burst of work and sleeps, and a desktop that ignores logind idle
  inhibitors sleeps silently. The hold was measured on Linux only; on Windows and macOS CI proves the request
  is registered (`powercfg /requests`, `pmset -g assertions`), not that the machine stays up.
- **The two-cards-one-conversation warning reaches only the providers that report an in-app switch**
  (`internal/terminal/terminal.go` `reportDuplicate`, `native/cmd/lich-native/duplicate.go`): lich learns
  which conversation a card runs from its session-start report, so a resume typed inside the agent's own app
  is warned about only once that report names the new id. Some report it only with their next prompt or tool
  call, so a turn may already have run in both cards, and Cursor CLI and opencode report nothing at all: their
  row keeps the old id and a restart resumes the conversation the card opened with (each provider's version:
  `docs/providers/`, Hooks). Reopening from lich itself is not this gap: every door through `store.reopen`
  focuses the card that holds the conversation.
- **Only a Claude Code session whose mod polls can be driven, asked, or report for itself** (`spawn.Control`,
  `spawn.Ask`, `internal/terminal/modcontrol.go`, `modusage.go`, `modstatus.go`; each contract in `docs/hooks/`,
  mod-control, mod-usage, mod-status and session-state, has its own Known ceilings): mods are a Claude Code
  feature, from 2.1.280 and only with the lich-plugin mod loaded, 0.15.0 or newer. The other seven providers, and
  a Claude Code session without the mod, have nothing that runs inside them and polls. So `lich control` and
  `lich ask` refuse them by provider before anything is queued (no other CLI exposes a fork of its own
  conversation to anything running inside it), their readout stays the one lich derives, their errands show only
  in the card's tooltip and inbox mark, and a compaction keeps the finished turn's check or is a spinner with no
  tool line, which reads as a stuck turn. The traps a caller walks into:
  - `/model` and `/effort` are refused as slash commands: run through a mod they write `~/.claude/settings.json`,
    the default for every new session (2.1.288). The `model` and `effort` actions are the per-session route.
  - A slash command that opens a dialog (`/cost`) holds that session's later slash commands until someone
    presses Esc in its terminal; lich cannot tell such a command apart before running it.
  - A session cannot ask itself, nor control itself past `model` and `effort`: an abort would end the asking turn,
    a prompt or a slash command would only run after it, and a question would ride the request it is waiting on.
  - An ask knows the conversation only as of the last finished model response, cannot be cancelled (past lich's
    90 seconds the fork runs on, billed, and its answer is dropped), never reaches the session's cost, and is cut
    at 16,000 characters (2.1.289).
  - A reported readout wins over the derived one, so two sessions on the same model can disagree by the requests
    no transcript records (2.7% and 3.1% of a session's cost on 2.1.289). Its cost replaces the conversation's
    ledger row and drops its sub-agent rows, so a lich restarted before the session's first report re-scans that
    conversation from the transcript until the report lands again. Only a long-lived token login's plan gauge
    uses the reported rate limits: a credentials login keeps its usage route, which names the plan, the account
    and the model-scoped caps a report does not carry.
  - An errand sent privately (a subagent or workflow step inside the session) never shows on the status line,
    since the session's own collect never reaches it.
